talks.originalTitle: 从开源软件到开源智能：硅基时间正在重写开发者世界

title.en: From Open-Source Software to Open Intelligence: Silicon Time Is Rewriting the Developer World
title.zh: 从开源软件到开源智能：硅基时间正在重写开发者世界

talks.slug: p-124-从开源软件到开源智能-硅基时间正在重写开发者世界
talks.originalAbstract: AI 正在把开源从“软件协作”推向“智能协作”。当代码生成、Agent 与自主执行开始进入开发全流程，开发者创造软件的方式、开源社区的协作模式，以及人与机器的角色边界都在被重新定义。本次分享将从“硅基时间”的视角，探讨开源如何从代码与软件走向模型、Agent 与智能系统，以及这场变化将为开发者带来怎样的新机会。

overview.en: AI is pushing open source from software collaboration toward intelligence collaboration. This keynote explores how code generation, agents, and autonomous execution are redefining software creation, community collaboration, and the boundary between developers and machines—and what new opportunities this shift creates.
overview.zh: AI 正推动开源从“软件协作”走向“智能协作”。本次主旨演讲探讨代码生成、智能体与自主执行如何重新定义软件创造、社区协作及人与机器的边界，并分析这场变化为开发者带来的新机会。

talks.originalTitle: Self-Evolving Apps: Building Software That Gets Smarter Every Time You Use It

title.en: Self-Evolving Apps: Building Software That Gets Smarter Every Time You Use It
title.zh: 自进化应用：构建每次使用都会变得更智能的软件

talks.originalAbstract:
Most apps are built once and stay the same. Self-evolving apps are different, they improve every time you use them, not because someone updates the code, but because the app learns from your corrections.

This intelligence exists completely outside the app as a separate, updatable layer. Before each use, it reads your previous corrections and uses them as examples to make better decisions. No machine learning required, neither retraining or data science team. 

Drawn from several apps running in daily production, this talk shares what self-evolving apps are, how to design them, how to build one, which licensing models work best and the lessons I have learned from building several of these apps, as well as a live demonstration.

overview.en: Self-evolving apps improve with each use by learning from user corrections, not through code updates. This intelligence operates as a separate, updatable layer that uses past corrections to enhance decision-making without requiring machine learning or data science teams. The talk covers design, development, licensing models, and lessons learned from real-world applications.
overview.zh: 自进化应用通过学习用户的修正来不断改进，而不是通过代码更新。这种智能以独立可更新的层形式存在，利用过往修正提升决策能力，无需机器学习或数据科学团队。本次演讲将介绍自进化应用的设计、开发、授权模式及实际应用中的经验教训。

talks.originalTitle: Network-Sourced AI: Open Ensembles, Private Data, and a Reproducible Path to the Frontier

title.en: Network-Sourced AI: Open Ensembles, Private Data, and a Reproducible Path to the Frontier
title.zh: 网络源生 AI：开放集成、私有数据与通往前沿的可复现路径

talks.originalAbstract: Frontier AI has become concentrated in a handful of closed labs, and public benchmarks tell us little about how models actually perform on real work — scores are frozen on publication day, easily gamed, and blind to the private, domain-specific data where the largest capability gains live. This talk presents "Network-Sourced AI," the open-source approach developed by the OpenMined Foundation to change that. Its foundation is multi-model ensembling: combining the answers of diverse models — open and closed, large and small — to systematically outperform any single model. On top of this, OpenMined applies Structured Transparency and attribution-based control, so every result is publicly reproducible and data owners retain full control over which evaluations remote models may perform on their data, protected by Privacy-Enhancing Technologies. I will show a demonstration of our newly launched open-source toolkit and public leaderboard, show how anyone can build, run, and reproduce state-of-the-art ensembles on their own machine using the AI subscriptions they already pay for, and discuss how data owners can turn private archives into community benchmarks without the data ever leaving their control.

overview.en: Network-Sourced AI, developed by the OpenMined Foundation, addresses the limitations of closed AI labs by using open ensembles of diverse models to improve performance. It combines Structured Transparency and Privacy-Enhancing Technologies to ensure reproducibility and data control. The talk demonstrates an open-source toolkit and public leaderboard, enabling users to build and reproduce state-of-the-art models locally while maintaining data privacy.
overview.zh: OpenMined基金会开发的Network-Sourced AI通过结合多种模型的开放集成，解决了封闭AI实验室的局限性。它采用结构化透明度和隐私增强技术，确保结果可复现且数据所有者能控制数据使用。演讲展示了新的开源工具包和公开排行榜，使用户能在本地使用已有AI订阅构建和复现最先进的模型，同时保持数据隐私。

talks.originalTitle: AI-Native Company Operating System: How Open Source Agents Transform Startup Workflows

title.en: AI-Native Company Operating System: How Open Source Agents Transform Startup Workflows
title.zh: AI 原生公司操作系统：开源智能体如何重塑初创企业工作流

talks.originalAbstract:
AI is not just changing how we build software — it is changing how companies are organized.

Traditional organizations are built around human roles, processes, and software tools. AI-native organizations take a different approach: knowledge becomes structured memory, AI agents become collaborative workers, and workflows become intelligent systems that continuously learn and improve.

In this talk, Jacky Hsu, founder of Ingora and former Microsoft product leader, will share practical lessons from building an AI-native company developing Qrio, an AI learning companion for children and families.

The talk explores how a small startup team combines open-source technologies, AI agents, coding assistants, and knowledge systems to create an organization that can move from strategy and ideas to product design, engineering execution, and operational learning with unprecedented speed.
Rather than treating AI as isolated productivity tools, this session presents a vision of the company itself becoming an AI-powered operating system — where humans provide creativity, judgment, and vision, while AI agents amplify execution and organizational intelligence.

overview.en: AI is transforming how companies are organized, moving from traditional human-centric structures to AI-native systems where knowledge is structured memory and workflows become intelligent, self-improving systems. Jacky Hsu will discuss how Ingora leverages open-source agents, coding assistants, and knowledge systems to rapidly develop Qrio, an AI learning companion for children and families. This approach treats the company itself as an AI-powered operating system, enhancing execution and organizational intelligence through AI agents.
overview.zh: AI 正在改变企业的组织方式：企业正从传统、以人为中心的结构，转向把知识作为结构化记忆、把工作流构建为智能且持续改进的系统。Jacky Hsu 将分享 Ingora 如何利用开源智能体、编程助手和知识系统，快速开发面向儿童与家庭的 AI 学习伙伴 Qrio。这种方法把公司本身视为由 AI 驱动的操作系统，并通过智能体提升执行能力与组织智能。

talks.originalTitle: Your AI Product Is Ready. Is Your Company Ready for Europe?

title.en: Your AI Product Is Ready. Is Your Company Ready for Europe?
title.zh: 你的 AI 产品准备好了，你的公司准备好进入欧洲了吗？

talks.originalAbstract:
Europe represents one of the world's most attractive markets for AI companies. But for companies building and scaling AI products in Asia, entering Europe is no longer simply a question of finding customers, partners, or investors.
The European AI market is increasingly shaped by regulatory requirements, governance expectations, and new responsibilities for organisations developing, providing, deploying, or distributing AI systems.
For AI companies looking to expand internationally, the challenge is therefore not only to build a great AI product, but to understand whether the company, product, governance model, and operational processes are ready for the European market.
This session introduces a practical approach to EU AI Market Entry Readiness, exploring the key questions AI companies should address before scaling into Europe.
What is the regulatory status of your AI system? What role does your company play in the AI value chain? Could your system fall into a high-risk category? What governance, documentation, transparency, human oversight, and risk management requirements may apply? And what should companies consider before entering the European market rather than discovering regulatory challenges after they have already signed their first European customer?
The session will also explore how emerging technologies, including Agentic AI and increasingly autonomous systems, may create new governance and market-entry considerations.
The session will explore what European market entry really means for companies building AI outside Europe, and why regulatory readiness is becoming part of the journey, not an afterthought. The conversation will connect AI innovation, product strategy, governance, and international expansion, with a focus on the questions companies should be asking before they set their sights on the European market.
Because talking about regulation does not have to be boring. The goal is to challenge some common assumptions, bring a fresh perspective to the European AI market, and leave the audience thinking differently about what it really takes to take an AI product from Asia to Europe.

overview.en: Europe is a highly attractive market for AI companies, but entering it requires more than just a great product. Companies must ensure their governance, operations, and compliance are ready for Europe's regulatory environment. This session explores key questions AI firms should address before expanding into Europe, including regulatory status, risk categories, and governance requirements. It also discusses how emerging technologies like Agentic AI may influence market entry strategies and regulatory readiness.
overview.zh: 欧洲是AI公司极具吸引力的市场，但进入该市场不仅需要优秀的产品，还需要确保公司治理、运营和合规性符合欧洲的监管环境。本次演讲将探讨AI公司扩展至欧洲前应考虑的关键问题，包括监管状态、风险类别和治理要求。此外，还将讨论像Agentic AI等新兴技术如何影响市场进入策略和监管准备。

talks.originalTitle: The Sovereignty Layer: Why Open Source Is How the Global South Shapes AI

title.en: The Sovereignty Layer: Why Open Source Is How the Global South Shapes AI
title.zh: 主权层：为什么开源是全球南方塑造 AI 的方式

talks.originalAbstract:
The most powerful technology in human history is being shaped by a handful of companies, in a handful of cities, in a handful of languages. For most of humanity — women, the Global South, non-technical creators — the only role on offer is to consume what others decide. This is the defining risk of the AI era: not that machines will think, but that so few humans will hold the pen that writes our shared future.

Open source is the most powerful answer we have. But open weights and open code are necessary, not sufficient. If the people who use AI have no voice in how it's governed, "open" becomes a technical detail rather than a democratic reality. The missing layer isn't another framework — it's a structured way to turn millions of users into co-authors.

Drawing on my own path — born in Indonesia, the first and only Indonesian woman admitted to France's elite ENA (and only the third Indonesian ever), then a front-row witness to the launch of the current AI boom in Silicon Valley — I'll argue that open source and global participation are two halves of the same fight. One opens the technology; the other opens the decision.

I'll introduce the model behind Global AI Assembly and its three pillars: (1) Educate — short, hands-on AI training that turns non-technical people into builders, because you no longer need to be an engineer, you need to be curious; (2) Give Voice — structuring learners' real opinions, concerns, and needs into rigorous reports; and (3) Shape — carrying those citizen voices to governments, companies, and standards bodies so AI is built with people, not merely for them. With hubs from Paris to West Africa, this is open-source thinking applied not just to models, but to governance itself.

This talk is for the builders in the room who sense that the open-source movement is about more than performance benchmarks — that it is, at its heart, a fight over who gets to decide. I'll offer a concrete framework for how the open-source community can become the infrastructure of a genuinely democratic AI: sovereign, inclusive, and globally co-authored. Attendees will leave with a new lens on their own work — not as engineers optimizing a stack, but as architects of who the future belongs to. The question is no longer whether AI will change the world. It is: who holds the pen?

overview.en: The talk discusses how open source can empower the Global South in shaping AI governance. It introduces the Global AI Assembly model, which focuses on education, giving voice to users, and influencing AI development through structured participation. The speaker argues that open source is not just about code but about democratizing decision-making in AI.
overview.zh: 本次演讲探讨开源如何帮助全球南方参与塑造 AI 治理。演讲将介绍 Global AI Assembly 模式及其三大支柱：教育非技术人群、汇集用户声音，并通过结构化参与影响政府、企业和标准组织。演讲者认为，开源不只是开放代码与权重，更是让更多人共同参与 AI 决策的基础。

talks.originalTitle: Building a Knowledge-Work Harness: From Coding Agents to Executable Strategy

title.en: Building a Knowledge-Work Harness: From Coding Agents to Executable Strategy
title.zh: 构建知识工作 Harness：从编程智能体到可执行战略

talks.originalAbstract:
Coding harnesses work because code carries its own verifier: tests, compilers, type systems. An agent can run until something passes. Knowledge work has none of that — no compiler for a decision, no test suite for a strategy, and "done" is a judgment call. Building an agent harness for knowledge work is a vastly different problem than building one for code, and most of what the ecosystem has learned does not transfer cleanly.

This talk is a field report from a year of building and running one. I am a strategist, not a developer, and my one-person consultancy operates day to day on an open-source, local-first agent fleet: local models, flat-rate delegation, no cloud dependencies.

What the talk covers:

- Component by component, what survives the move from coding harness to knowledge-work harness — skills, memory, delegation, review gates — and what breaks. The verification gap is the organizing problem: what stands in for the test suite when the output is a decision.
- The layer that makes the harness work: strategy written as a protocol. Plain-text decision rules, closed schemas, and gates that both the human and the agents operate under — the firm's strategy as the harness's operating instructions, and the nearest thing knowledge work has to a verifier.
- Failure modes from daily production use: where plain text is enough, where it is not, and what a year of operation did to the strategy itself.

The talk includes a live demo: an agent reading the strategy files and making a gated decision, running locally on open-source infrastructure.

overview.en: Building a knowledge-work harness requires addressing the verification gap, as decisions lack the automated checks found in coding. This talk shares insights from a year of running an open-source, local-first agent system, focusing on components that survive the transition and the role of strategy as a protocol. A live demo illustrates an agent making a gated decision based on plain-text rules.
overview.zh: 构建知识工作框架需要解决验证缺口，因为决策缺乏代码中的自动检查。本次演讲分享了一年运行开源本地优先智能体系统的经验，探讨了组件迁移中的关键要素及策略作为协议的作用。演示展示了基于纯文本规则的智能体如何在本地基础设施上做出受控决策。

talks.originalTitle: Accelerating Algorithm Autoresearch

title.en: Accelerating Algorithm Autoresearch
title.zh: 加速算法自动研究

talks.originalAbstract:
Optimizing software has never been easier with the advent of agentic AI... right? It turns out it's not quite that simple!

Autoresearch is a powerful technique for optimization; an agent iteratively modifies, tests, and benchmarks changes to the codebase with the goal of maximizing the benchmark score.

While powerful, this process faces challenges, especially at scale:
- Cheating / reward hacking (just as in reinforcement learning).
- Overfitting to benchmark's inputs.
- Tradeoffs between input breadth and build/test/benchmark cost.
- Local maximums.

In this talk, we'll discuss some of these challenges and how to overcome them, based on examples from the open source GPUMODE kernel competitions and infrastructure.
We'll explore how to take autoresearch results from "cool idea" to "shipped in production".

overview.en: Optimizing software with agentic AI is more complex than it seems. Autoresearch, which uses agents to iteratively modify and test code, faces challenges like reward hacking and overfitting. This talk explores these issues and how to turn autoresearch results into production-ready solutions, using examples from open-source GPU kernel competitions and infrastructure.
overview.zh: 利用智能体 AI 优化软件比想象中复杂。Autoresearch 通过智能体迭代修改和测试代码，但面临奖励作弊（reward hacking）、过拟合等挑战。本次演讲将结合开源 GPU 内核竞赛和基础设施的实例，探讨这些问题以及如何将 Autoresearch 成果转化为生产可用的方案。

talks.originalTitle: Agent-Centric Engineering — From Personal Productivity to Organizational Capability

title.en: Agent-Centric Engineering — From Personal Productivity to Organizational Capability
title.zh: 以智能体为中心的工程实践——从个人生产力到组织能力

talks.originalAbstract:
Talk Abstract: Agent-Centric Engineering — From Personal Productivity to Organizational Capability
Speaker: Dong Xin, Huawei Cangjie Programming Language Team
Former Microsoft Azure enterprise cloud expert and lead of Huawei's mobile AI tooling, Ascend MindStudio, HarmonyOS DevEco Studio, and the Cangjie/Bisheng C language IDE. Since early 2025, Dong Xin has pioneered AI Agent-driven R&D models and open-sourced ACEHarness, now adopted by multiple large-scale engineering teams.
The Shift: AI development has entered its second half. The challenge is no longer "coding faster alone," but how organizations restructure roles, redefine quality boundaries, and compose teams for Agent-centric workflows.
Three Pillars:
ACE (Agent-Centric Engineering): Engineers ascend from coders to Directors (orchestration), Screenwriters (specification), and Quality Arbiters (trust).
Human IO Loop: Human On the Loop for systemic control; Human In the Loop for result trust. Human attention focuses on objectives, boundaries, and risks—Agent executes autonomously.
ATM (Ability-based Task Matching): Dynamic task allocation to optimal executors.
The Cangjie Journey: From localized trials to organizational capability, with measurable gains in library development, crash analysis, documentation, API testing, and code review.
Two Battlefield Stories:
Compiler Memory Optimization (high-coupling): Pre-defined objectives and boundaries let the Agent autonomously design, implement, and self-repair—humans govern and accept at critical nodes.
Hash Library Performance (high-knowledge-density): A strike team of "Expert + Intern + Agent" delivered results while converting expertise into reusable knowledge assets.
ACEHarness: An open-source platform bridging team experience to engineering infrastructure—featuring Spec-Driven Development, state-machine workflows, intelligent Supervisor routing, adversarial iteration, multi-Agent deliberation, Git audit baselines, and long-term memory with skill extensibility.
Takeaway: A concrete framework for moving from AI tool adoption to Agent-centric organizational capability, with actionable patterns for human-AI governance and quality boundary definition.

overview.en: Agent-Centric Engineering (ACE) transforms individual productivity into organizational capability by redefining roles and workflows. Dong Xin introduced ACEHarness, an open-source platform enabling Spec-Driven Development and multi-Agent collaboration, with real-world applications in compiler optimization and hash library performance. The framework emphasizes human-AI governance and quality boundary definition for effective AI agent integration.
overview.zh: 以Agent为中心的工程（ACE）通过重新定义角色和工作流程，将个人生产力转化为组织能力。董鑫介绍了ACEHarness这一开源平台，支持基于规范的开发和多Agent协作，并在编译器优化和哈希库性能等实际应用中取得成效。该框架强调人机治理和质量边界定义，为AI 智能体集成提供可操作的模式。

talks.originalTitle: State of harness engineering

title.en: State of Harness Engineering
title.zh: Harness 工程现状

talks.originalAbstract: Coding agents are getting better fast, but many teams are discovering that better models and a pile of markdown instructions don't automatically mean they can lean back and reduce supervision. Harness engineering is the set of practices coding agent users have to shape how their agent behaves and how reliable its output is. Markdown instructions are part of it, but so are the controls and automated feedback loops built around the agent. This talk lays out a mental model for the harness engineering toolbox, then walks through the current landscape of practices, with a focus on giving agents feedback sensors.

overview.en: State of harness engineering explores the challenges of effectively managing coding agents. While models improve, teams find that better models alone aren't enough; they need structured practices to guide and refine agent behavior. The talk introduces a mental model for harness engineering, emphasizing feedback mechanisms and control systems to enhance reliability.
overview.zh: 本次演讲探讨了编程智能体的有效管理挑战。尽管模型性能不断提升，但团队发现仅依靠更强大的模型并不足够，还需系统性的实践来引导和优化智能体行为。演讲介绍了 harness engineering 的思维模型，重点强调反馈机制和控制系统以提升可靠性。

talks.originalTitle: AI时代网络安全的“矛”与“盾”

title.en: The “Spear” and “Shield” of Cybersecurity in the AI Era
title.zh: AI 时代网络安全的“矛”与“盾”

talks.originalAbstract:
我长期扎根于一线攻防实战，对AI如何重塑攻击链有切身体会。本次分享不空谈趋势，而是基于奇安信等一线安全公司的实战数据与最新案例，提供一套可落地、可复用的建设路径，希望能为现场的同仁提供真正的决策参考。
作为网络安全一线从业者，我深切感受到AI技术正在将网络攻防推向一个前所未有的“失衡”临界点。本次分享将结合近期发生的重大安全事件与前沿洞察，提出一套从战略到落地的“再平衡”解决方案，希望能与参会同仁共同探讨。
核心观点与内容大纲：
1. 警惕“工业化”攻击：Mythos与漏洞“军备竞赛”
我将首次在公开论坛深度剖析Anthropic旗下Mythos模型带来的范式级冲击。它实现了从漏洞挖掘到攻击执行的全自动流水线作业，将资深工程师数天的工作压缩至分钟级。这导致漏洞产出速度（分钟级）与补丁修复速度（平均72天）之间出现致命性“时差”，彻底打破了传统攻防博弈的平衡。
引用“玻璃翼计划”等案例，揭示当前攻击高效化、自动化、平民化的三大趋势，以及由此引发的全球关基领域系统性焦虑。
2. 防守“力不从心”：传统安全体系的三大崩溃
人的上限 vs AI的无限： 我们的人海战术、静态规则，在AI驱动的恶意代码变异、高频次攻击和全域扫描面前，已经形同虚设。
“内忧外患”加剧： 我将分享双重勒索、供应链攻击（如“DeepSeek”恶意包事件）、数据泄露（如科研机构违规用AI工具泄密） 等真实案例。这些案例无一不指向一个核心问题：安全孤岛化、单点化的防守体系，无法应对体系化、智能化的攻击。
3. 破局之道：从“追着漏洞跑”到“带着漏洞防”
核心观点：我们无法阻止漏洞被挖出，但可以重构防御体系，让攻击者“即使挖了洞，也打不进来，进得来也拿不走，拿走了也用不了”。
【三位一体】内生安全纵深防御体系： 我将详细阐述如何通过高位情报AI化、中位运营智能体化、低位产品MCP化，实现安全能力的协同联动。

4. 总结与展望：
网络安全已进入“体系对抗”时代。我们必须借鉴“社会治安综合治理”的网格化理念，通过一体化安全改造，让安全从“追着漏洞跑”的被动修补，转变为“带着漏洞防”的主动防御。
最终，安全不再是成本，而是数字化业务发展的底座和竞争力。

overview.en: Drawing on frontline cybersecurity experience, the speaker explains how AI is reshaping attack chains and presents a practical framework based on real-world data and cases from QI-ANXIN and other security companies. The talk examines the imbalance created by AI-driven attacks and proposes a "rebalance" strategy for moving from reactive patching to proactive defense.
overview.zh: 该演讲者长期参与一线攻防实战，分享AI如何重塑攻击链，并基于奇安信等公司实战数据提出可落地的建设路径。演讲聚焦AI引发的攻防失衡问题，提出从战略到落地的“再平衡”方案，旨在推动防御体系从被动修补转向主动防御。

talks.originalTitle: Mapping the Open Agentic AI Landscape: From Open Models to Cross-Foundation Architectures

title.en: Mapping the Open Agentic AI Landscape: From Open Models to Cross-Foundation Architectures
title.zh: 绘制开放智能体 AI 全景图：从开放模型到跨基金会架构

talks.originalAbstract:
As autonomous AI agents shift from experimental projects to production workloads, scaling them requires navigating a rapidly expanding open-source landscape. True technical sovereignty demands an open stack where transparent, open-weight models are backed by an open supply chain to establish verifiable trust. Managing multi-turn agentic loops requires seamless integration across open models, compute, orchestration, and agent protocols.

This landscape presentation maps the end-to-end open agentic ecosystem. At the substrate level, the PyTorch Foundation powers compute and model serving by hosting Ray for distributed execution alongside vLLM for high-throughput, memory-efficient serving. The CNCF delivers platform orchestration through Kubernetes, cloud-native agentic standards, and evolving AI Gateways that provide smart routing across a mixture of models while integrating agent harnesses directly into the platform. Finally, the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) standardizes tool execution and agent delegation via MCP and A2A specifications. 

Attendees will gain a comprehensive map of how these layers intersect to deliver a secure, sovereign alternative to proprietary AI stacks.

overview.en: The talk explores the open agentic AI landscape, emphasizing the need for transparent, open-weight models and an open supply chain to ensure technical sovereignty. It outlines the ecosystem, including PyTorch Foundation, CNCF, and AAIF, which together enable secure, scalable agentic systems through integrated compute, orchestration, and protocol standards.
overview.zh: 本次演讲梳理开放智能体 AI 的生态系统，强调透明度、开放权重模型和开放供应链对技术主权的重要性。演讲介绍 PyTorch 基金会、CNCF 和 AAIF 等生态组成部分，以及它们如何整合计算、编排和协议标准，共同支撑安全、可扩展的智能体系统。

talks.originalTitle: Cangjie and the New Frontier of Programming Languages in the AI Era

title.en: Cangjie and the New Frontier of Programming Languages in the AI Era
title.zh: 仓颉与 AI 时代编程语言的新前沿

talks.originalAbstract:
In the AI era, program execution has evolved into a "CPU + LLM Co-execution" paradigm. Programming languages must now serve two masters: human developers and AI Agents. This talk explores how the Cangjie language is being reimagined for AI-native affinity.
AI-Friendly Infrastructure Overhaul
Zhan outlines a three-pronged transformation of Cangjie's toolchain: upgrading the compiler, LSP, and testing framework to become first-class citizens for AI consumption; building a tree-structured AI skill library (knowledge base) for structured capability reuse; and introducing Speclang, a semi-formal design description language that translates natural language requirements into verifiable specification constraints—directly addressing the core pain point of intent ambiguity in AI coding.
Toward a New Agent Language
Looking beyond today's languages, the lab is prototyping a novel Agent Language that balances deterministic CPU execution with the flexible reasoning of large models. The design targets workflow programming, fine-grained context control, and visual multi-Agent collaboration—enabling a new class of software where human intent, formal verification, and LLM improvisation coexist in a single executable fabric.
Audience Takeaway
Attendees will gain insight into how programming languages are being reinvented for the "CPU + LLM" era, with concrete examples of AI-friendly infrastructure, intent-formalization techniques, and a glimpse of the emerging Agent-oriented programming paradigm.

overview.en: As software moves toward CPU and LLM co-execution, programming languages must serve both developers and AI agents. This talk presents Cangjie's AI-friendly compiler, LSP and testing infrastructure, a structured skill library, Speclang for verifiable specifications, and early work on an Agent-oriented language.
overview.zh: 随着软件进入 CPU 与大模型协同执行的新阶段，编程语言需要同时服务开发者与 AI 智能体。本次演讲介绍仓颉面向 AI 的编译器、LSP、测试基础设施、结构化技能库、可验证规格语言 Speclang，以及智能体语言的早期探索。

talks.originalTitle: Evaluation You Can Audit: Eclipse PanEval as Shared Infrastructure

title.en: Evaluation You Can Audit: Eclipse PanEval as Shared Infrastructure
title.zh: 可审计的评测：Eclipse PanEval 作为共享基础设施

talks.originalAbstract:
Every team building AI depends on evaluation. Almost nobody controls the evaluation they depend on.
Benchmarks arrive as published numbers. The harness, the data, and the scoring logic often stay closed. That makes a result something you accept rather than verify.
Eclipse PanEval is an open source framework for evaluating large language and vision models. It began as a foundational contribution from the Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence. It is now moving to meritocratic stewardship at the Eclipse Foundation, where more than 440 open source projects are hosted under vendor-neutral governance.
The architecture is deliberately decoupled. Regions can evolve their evaluation sets, languages, and priorities independently, while staying technically synchronised with the global project. That is what makes shared evaluation infrastructure workable across regions that will never agree on everything.
I will cover what we built with BAAI, what it taught us about cross-region open source governance, and where the project needs contributors next.
I have spent 13 years building AI systems, and spoke about PanEval at GOSIM Paris this year. This session is the next chapter, from the infrastructure side.
You will leave knowing how to evaluate models on infrastructure you can audit, and how to help build it.

overview.en: This session presents Eclipse PanEval, an open-source framework for auditable evaluation of language and vision models. It explains its decoupled architecture, cross-region collaboration model, vendor-neutral governance, and how contributors can help build shared evaluation infrastructure.
overview.zh: 本次演讲介绍用于语言与视觉模型可审计评测的开源框架 Eclipse PanEval，讲解其解耦架构、跨区域协作方式、中立治理模式，以及社区如何共同建设共享评测基础设施。

talks.originalTitle: 2026，AI眼镜的“记忆拐点”

title.en: 2026: The Memory Inflection Point for AI Glasses
title.zh: 2026，AI 眼镜的“记忆拐点”

talks.originalAbstract:
In 2026, AI glasses are moving from early-adopter novelty to the mass market. At the same time, the competitive battleground is shifting from "feature count" to "memory depth." In the era of AI Agents, long-term memory is evolving from a mere product feature into a core capability of AI infrastructure. The "memory inflection point" has arrived – whoever helps users truly "remember" will define the next generation of AI glasses.
2026年，AI眼镜从小众尝鲜迈入大众市场。与此同时，行业竞争重心正从“功能数量”转向“记忆深度”。AI Agent时代，长期记忆正在从产品功能升级为AI基础设施的核心能力。“记忆拐点”已经到来——谁能帮用户“记住”，谁就能定义下一代AI眼镜。

overview.en: As AI glasses move toward the mass market, competition is shifting from the number of features to the depth of memory. This talk argues that long-term memory is becoming core AI infrastructure and may define the next generation of wearable agents.
overview.zh: 随着 AI 眼镜走向大众市场，竞争重点正从“功能数量”转向“记忆深度”。本次演讲探讨长期记忆如何成为 AI 基础设施的核心能力，并定义下一代可穿戴智能体。

talks.originalTitle: AI 原生组织的构建（Building the AI-Native Organization）

title.en: Building the AI-Native Organization
title.zh: AI 原生组织的构建

talks.originalAbstract:
先问一个最朴素的问题：组织为什么存在。因为工作要交给能干的执行单元，而过去能干活的只有人，所以才有了团队、层级和流程。现在这个前提变了，执行能力可以被复制、边际成本趋近于零，组织的最小单元就从一支团队变成一个人加一支 Agent 团队。
顺着这个前提往下推三步。第一步，人手里剩下的是不可替代的两成：判断、品味、在场、关系、手艺，个人价值等于关系加手艺，再乘以判断加品味加在场，两边缺一边就归零。第二步，管理动作从管人变成分活、定义、验收，做过三次的事应该写成 SOP，做过五次的事应该被 AI 接管。第三步，公司结构从串行的流程变成并行的网络，不停把串行的瓶颈压掉，这也是第三代公司和前两代最大的区别。
在自己公司里跑通只是一半。要让它在别人的生意里也成立，得有人把这套东西开进客户的真实业务，这就是 FDE。对内，AI 原生组织落到每个人身上就是 FDE 这种能力，做商业化、做产品、做研发都要有；对外，FDE 是把 AI 员工送上岗、并对业务结果负责的那一环。句子互动 2023 年就开始按结果交付，比硅谷把这个岗位炒热早了三年。支撑它的是 7 大产品基建 × FDE · 三层一体：模型是发动机，七大产品基建是整车工程，FDE 是把整车开进客户业务的那一环。一套基建复制到多个岗位和多个行业，交付按业务结果衡量，不按项目人头衡量。
这场分享会用真实落地经验回答四个问题：哪些流程值得交给 Agent，人和 Agent 的责任边界怎么划，收益怎么衡量，以及合规要求高的行业里怎么让 Agent 可控上线。

Start with the plainest question: why do organizations exist. Because work has to go to a unit that can execute it, and for all of history the only such unit was a person, which is where teams, hierarchies and processes come from. That premise has changed. Execution can now be copied at close to zero marginal cost, so the smallest unit of an organization shifts from a team to one person plus a team of agents.
Three consequences follow. First, what stays with people is the irreplaceable twenty percent: judgment, taste, presence, relationships and craft. Personal value is relationships plus craft, multiplied by judgment plus taste plus presence, and it collapses to zero if either side is missing. Second, management becomes assigning the work, defining what done means, and accepting the result. Anything done three times should become an SOP, and anything done five times should be taken over by AI. Third, the company moves from a serial process to a parallel network with the serial bottlenecks squeezed out, which is what separates a third generation company from the two that came before it.
Proving this inside your own company is only half the job. For it to hold inside someone else business, a person has to drive it into their real operations, and that is FDE. Internally, an AI-native organization comes down to FDE as a capability that commercial, product and engineering people all need. Externally, FDE is the part that puts AI employees to work and owns the business outcome. Juzi.bot started delivering against results in 2023, three years before the role became the hottest job in Silicon Valley. Underneath sits seven product infrastructures working as one across three layers, with FDE running through them. The model is the engine, the seven infrastructures are the whole vehicle engineering, and FDE drives that vehicle into the customer business. One set of infrastructure replicates across roles and industries, and delivery is measured by business outcomes rather than project headcount.
Drawing on real deployments, the talk answers four questions: which workflows are worth handing to agents, where the responsibility line between people and agents sits, how return is measured, and how agents go live in a controlled way in regulated industries.

overview.en: Drawing on real enterprise deployments, this talk explores how organizations change when execution can be delegated to teams of agents. It covers the new human role, management through task definition and acceptance, parallel organizational structures, FDE capabilities, and controlled agent deployment in regulated industries.
overview.zh: 本次演讲结合真实企业落地经验，探讨当执行能力可以交给智能体团队后，组织结构将如何变化。内容涵盖人的新角色、以任务定义和验收为核心的管理方式、并行组织、FDE 能力，以及合规行业中的可控智能体上线。

talks.originalTitle: Agent 产品范式创新的若干命题 Key Propositions for Agent Product Paradigm Innovation

title.en: Key Propositions for Innovation in the Agent Product Paradigm
title.zh: Agent 产品范式创新的若干命题

talks.originalAbstract:
本次演讲将跳出当前 Agent 产品的局部创新，从更长周期、更底层的视角，探讨一场正在发生的产品创新跃迁：Agent 改变的不只是产品形态，而是产品的整个范式。 当软件从被动响应走向主动行动，从功能交付走向能力生成，从一次性交付走向持续进化，产品的定义、价值、交互、商业模式与竞争壁垒等都将被重新书写。本次演讲将围绕这一变化提出一组核心命题，并尝试回答一个更根本的问题：当软件开始理解意图、主动行动并持续进化，Agent时代的产品范式究竟应该如何重新定义？

This talk looks beyond the incremental innovations of today’s Agent products and takes a longer-term, deeper perspective to explore a fundamental paradigm shift in product innovation: Agents are changing not just the form of products, but the very paradigm of products themselves. As software evolves from passive response to proactive action, from delivering functions to generating capabilities, and from one-time delivery to continuous evolution, the very definition of a product—its value, interaction model, business model, and competitive moat—will be fundamentally rewritten. This talk puts forward a set of core propositions around this transformation and seeks to answer a more fundamental question: As software begins to understand intent, act autonomously, and continuously evolve, how should we redefine the product paradigm in the Agent era?

overview.en: This talk looks beyond incremental Agent product features to examine a broader paradigm shift: software is moving from passive response to proactive action, from delivering fixed functions to generating capabilities, and from one-time delivery to continuous evolution. It explores how this shift will redefine product value, interaction, business models, and competitive advantage.
overview.zh: 本次演讲跳出 Agent 产品的局部功能创新，从更长周期和更底层的视角讨论产品范式的变化：软件正从被动响应走向主动行动，从功能交付走向能力生成，从一次性交付走向持续进化，并由此重新定义产品价值、交互方式、商业模式与竞争壁垒。

talks.originalTitle: KTransformers: The Fine-Tuning-to-Inference Closed Loop for Full-Precision 1T-Class MoE Models on Consumer Hardware

title.en: KTransformers: The Fine-Tuning-to-Inference Closed Loop for Full-Precision 1T-Class MoE Models on Consumer Hardware
title.zh: KTransformers：消费级硬件上全精度万亿参数级 MoE 模型的微调到推理闭环

talks.originalAbstract:
Frontier open-source MoE models are entering the 1T-parameter era, traditionally requiring data center GPU clusters for adaptation and deployment. KTransformers offers a low-cost alternative for 4090-class workstations using CPU-GPU heterogeneous co-compute. By offloading sparse MoE experts to CPU DRAM while keeping hot dense computation on a 24GB-class GPU, KTransformers enables efficient local inference.

More than just an inference engine, this architecture supports a complete workstation-level iteration loop: serving the model locally, collecting domain-specific feedback, fine-tuning LoRA adapters via LLaMA-Factory, and deploying the adapted model back to KTransformers. This approach provides small applied AI teams, university labs, and researchers a practical, parameter-efficient path to study, serve, and iterate on 1T-class models without prohibitive hardware costs.

overview.en: KTransformers enables efficient local inference for 1T-class MoE models on consumer hardware by leveraging CPU-GPU heterogeneous computing. It supports a full fine-tuning-to-inference loop, allowing model serving, feedback collection, and deployment back to the system. This approach makes large-scale model iteration accessible to small teams and researchers without high hardware costs.
overview.zh: KTransformers 通过利用 CPU-GPU 异构计算，在消费级硬件上实现了 1T 级 MoE 模型的高效本地推理。它支持从微调到推理的完整闭环，允许模型服务、反馈收集和部署回系统。这种方法使小型团队和研究人员能够在不需高昂硬件成本的情况下研究、服务和迭代大型模型。

talks.originalTitle: Agentic AI on Global Edge: Deploying SPEAR-Powered Operations Agents with MCP

title.en: Agentic AI on Global Edge: Deploying SPEAR-Powered Operations Agents with MCP
title.zh: 全球边缘环境中的智能体 AI：借助 MCP 部署由 SPEAR 驱动的运维智能体

talks.originalAbstract:
As ByteDance’s global edge infrastructure scales, centralized operations struggle with latency and fragmented edge scenarios. We built lightweight AI operations agents natively on the SPEAR edge platform, leveraging its built-in AI capabilities and native MCP support to rapidly ship purpose-built agents.
Deployed locally on edge nodes, these agents autonomously handle real-time cluster monitoring, root cause analysis and automated issue resolution without relying on central services, drastically cutting response latency and manual overhead.
In this talk, we deep-dive into SPEAR’s edge AI runtime architecture, MCP-enabled agent development patterns, and key engineering lessons from our global production rollout, including edge resource optimization and network resilience practices.

overview.en: ByteDance's global edge infrastructure faces challenges with centralized operations due to latency and fragmented scenarios. By deploying lightweight AI operations agents on the SPEAR platform with MCP support, they achieve real-time monitoring, root cause analysis, and automated resolution at the edge, reducing latency and manual effort. The talk covers SPEAR's edge AI architecture, MCP-based agent development, and production insights on resource optimization and network resilience.
overview.zh: 字节跳动的全球边缘基础设施面临集中式运维带来的延迟和场景碎片化问题。通过在 SPEAR 平台部署支持 MCP 的轻量级 AI 运维智能体，可在边缘端实现实时监控、根因分析和自动化处置，降低延迟与人工成本。本次演讲将介绍 SPEAR 的边缘 AI 运行架构、基于 MCP 的智能体开发模式，以及全球生产部署中的资源优化与网络韧性实践。

talks.originalTitle: DHttp: From Partial Connectivity to Omniconnectivity

title.en: DHttp: From Partial Connectivity to Omniconnectivity
title.zh: DHttp：从部分连接到全域互联

talks.originalAbstract: 智能体互联网时代，为什么需要新的互联网，传统的万维网又有哪些缺陷？回顾互联网的发展史，会发现传输层以下都是公平的——任何一个网络设备都有 IP 地址、MAC 地址，每个不同的软件和硬件都被平等地对待；然而到了应用层，就不公平了：域名并非任意设备都能拥有，DNS 仅服务于数据中心网络环境中的节点，这对移动网络、家庭网络中的边缘智能体一点都不公平！而这一切在万维网的 HTTP 协议提出来之时就注定了，服务端上升到云端，客户端下沉到边缘，两者从一出生阶级差异就存在了。然而，谁说边缘 AI 不是服务端呢？Agent 要调用的工具、数据和设备，往往不在云上，而在用户身边。DHttp 协议正是为了破解这一难题，为阶级平等而来。DHttp 并不是重新发明 Http，而是在QUIC 和 HTTP3 的基础上实现了点到点通信、端到端加密，扩展 DNS 协议使其支持泛端点网络地址，进而融合客户端与服务端为一体，客户端即服务端，让域名、私钥、证书这套完美的 TLS 身份普适化到任何一个边缘 AI 上。它们产生了奇妙的组合反应，天然具备身份认证、安全传输、数据完整性，轻松解决了通过堆砌冗杂设计才解决的一系列难题。DHttp 将为我们揭开两两之间皆可互连的“真互联”世界的帷幕，开启万智互联全新体验！

overview.en: DHttp addresses the limitations of traditional HTTP by enabling peer-to-peer communication and end-to-end encryption. It extends DNS to support universal endpoint addresses, allowing edge AI devices to act as both clients and servers, achieving true equality in network interactions. This protocol simplifies secure, identity-based communication across diverse networks, paving the way for a more interconnected future.
overview.zh: DHttp 解决了传统 HTTP 的局限性，实现了点对点通信和端到端加密。它扩展了 DNS 以支持泛端点网络地址，使边缘 AI 设备能够同时作为客户端和服务端，实现网络交互的真正平等。该协议通过简化安全、基于身份的通信，解决了复杂设计带来的诸多问题，为万物互联的未来铺平道路。

talks.originalTitle: OpenCV 5: What’s New—and How to Prepare Your Company for the Upgrade

title.en: OpenCV 5: What’s New—and How to Prepare Your Company for the Upgrade
title.zh: OpenCV 5：有哪些新变化，以及企业应如何为升级做好准备

talks.originalAbstract:
OpenCV 5 is the most consequential modernization of the world’s leading open-source computer vision library in years. This talk explains what changed, why it matters, and how engineering leaders can upgrade without disrupting production systems.

We will tour the new foundation—C++17 and Python 3 baselines, removal of legacy APIs, expanded data types, true 0D/1D arrays, and the reorganization of features, geometry, calibration, stereo, and point-cloud capabilities. We will then examine the radically revised DNN stack: a new inference engine with much broader modern ONNX support, dynamic shapes and subgraphs, optional ONNX Runtime integration, stronger CPU performance, and end-to-end building blocks for vision-language models. We will also highlight modern local features and matching, improved robust estimation, multi-camera calibration, and new 3D workflows.

The second half is a practical migration playbook for companies. Attendees will learn how to inventory dependencies, identify removed or relocated APIs, convert legacy Caffe and Darknet models to ONNX, benchmark CPU and GPU execution paths, build compatibility tests, run OpenCV 4 and 5 in parallel, stage deployment, monitor regressions, and preserve a rollback path. You will leave with a concrete checklist for deciding when to upgrade and reducing technical, operational, and organizational risk.

overview.en: OpenCV 5 represents a major modernization of the leading open-source computer vision library, introducing updates to its foundation, DNN stack, and local features. The talk provides a practical guide for companies to upgrade smoothly, including migration strategies and risk mitigation.
overview.zh: OpenCV 5 是近年来对领先开源计算机视觉库的重大现代化更新，包含基础架构、深度学习栈和局部特征的改进。本次演讲为公司提供了一套实用的升级指南，涵盖迁移策略和风险缓解方法。

talks.originalTitle: RustNN at the Edge: WebNN as Infrastructure for Local AI Agents

title.en: RustNN at the Edge: WebNN as Infrastructure for Local AI Agents
title.zh: 边缘端 RustNN：以 WebNN 作为本地 AI 智能体的基础设施

talks.originalAbstract:
AI agents promise autonomy, but today they are tethered to the cloud. Local inference is the bottleneck. Every agent needs to run
 models on whatever device the user has, and building that support from scratch is prohibitively expensive. RustNN and the W3C
 WebNN standard offer a practical solution: a single graph builder with an operator set designed to run on as many platforms as
 possible, from ONNX Runtime and CoreML to LiteRT and beyond.

 This talk shows what the RustNN ecosystem delivers today. We will cover the RustNN API and how it enables writing an ML workload
 once in Rust and running it in three environments: as a native application on your desktop, as a Node.js addon in a server or
 local process, or as a compiled WebAssembly module in a browser. All three share the same RustNN/WebNN runtime without forking
 the codebase. We will show how WebNN graphs are defined and executed in Rust, and how the same code hits hardware acceleration
 whether it is running on your desktop GPU, inside Node.js, or in a browser WebNN backend. Finally, we will discuss where the
 project is headed.

overview.en: RustNN and the W3C WebNN standard provide a unified solution for running AI agents locally. The RustNN ecosystem allows developers to write ML workloads once in Rust and deploy them across three environments: desktop, Node.js, and WebAssembly. This approach enables hardware acceleration across different platforms without code duplication.
overview.zh: RustNN 和 W3C WebNN 标准为本地运行 AI 智能体提供了统一的解决方案。RustNN 生态系统允许开发者在 Rust 中编写一次机器学习任务，并部署到桌面、Node.js 和 WebAssembly 三种环境中。这种方法可以在不同平台实现硬件加速，而无需代码重复。

talks.originalTitle: From Khronos AI Ecosystem Research Insights to Edge AI Inference with Vulkan

title.en: From Khronos AI Ecosystem Research Insights to Edge AI Inference with Vulkan
title.zh: 从 Khronos AI 生态研究洞察到基于 Vulkan 的边缘 AI 推理

This presentation explores insights from the Khronos AI Ecosystem Research Project, the open-source frameworks enabling AI inference using Vulkan today, and emerging trends in machine learning and neural graphics. We’ll show selected use cases where Vulkan-based AI inference is a strong fit, including texture compression, LLM inference, image upscaling, and frame interpolation.

overview.en: As AI and real-time graphics converge, portable AI inference is transitioning from research to real-world deployment. This talk presents insights from the Khronos AI Ecosystem Research Project, open-source frameworks for Vulkan-based AI inference, and emerging trends in machine learning and neural graphics. Use cases such as texture compression, LLM inference, image upscaling, and frame interpolation are highlighted.
overview.zh: 随着AI与实时图形技术的融合，便携式AI推理正从研究转向实际部署。本次演讲介绍了Khronos AI生态系统研究项目的关键洞察，以及当前基于Vulkan的AI推理开源框架和机器学习、神经图形领域的新兴趋势。展示了纹理压缩、LLM推理、图像超分和帧插值等适用Vulkan AI推理的典型应用场景。

talks.originalTitle: 端侧智能的技术发展与 MiniCPM 开源生态实践观察

title.en: The Evolution of On-Device Intelligence and Lessons from the MiniCPM Open-Source Ecosystem
title.zh: 端侧智能的技术发展与 MiniCPM 开源生态实践观察

talks.slug: p-105-端侧智能的技术发展与-minicpm-开源生态实践观察
talks.originalAbstract: 介绍端侧智能技术的发展现状和产业观察，以MiniCPM的开源生态实践为例深入探讨

overview.en: This talk surveys the current development of on-device intelligence and related industry trends. Using the MiniCPM open-source ecosystem as a case study, it examines practical lessons in building and growing edge AI capabilities.
overview.zh: 本次演讲梳理端侧智能技术的发展现状与产业趋势，并以 MiniCPM 开源生态为案例，探讨端侧 AI 能力建设与生态实践中的经验。

talks.originalTitle: How Do You Read a Million Tokens on Your Laptop? You Don't.

title.en: How Do You Read a Million Tokens on Your Laptop? You Don't.
title.zh: 如何在笔记本电脑上读取一百万个 Token？答案是：不要直接读

talks.originalAbstract: Agentic knowledge work — plan, query, read, verify, synthesize, cite — is a loop over a document corpus, and running it on device binds two constraints at once: weights and KV cache share a few gigabytes, fixing the model under 7B, and the loop compounds error multiplicatively exactly where small models are weakest. What makes this tractable is that the corpus is static and known before the loop starts: cache-augmented generation exploits this on the write path, precomputing the corpus KV cache at ingestion, while recursive language models exploit it on the read path, bounding context through recursion over corpus structure — one writes the corpus into memory, the other reads what the memory can't already answer. We test this where there is no network to fall back on: a 321M model producing cited legal analysis in Niger on a Raspberry Pi 5, and curriculum retrieval for Senegalese teachers on Android. Alongside the systems we are building the ruler — an evaluation layer retargeting knowledge-work benchmarks to on-device conditions, scoring groundedness and delivery within a real time budget. The talk shares early lessons from building both, including negative results from small models on constrained devices, where error-message fidelity, not feature coverage, proved the lever behind model self-repair.

overview.en: This session explores on-device agentic knowledge work under strict memory and model-size constraints. It combines cache-augmented generation, recursive language models, and grounded evaluation, with examples including cited legal analysis on a Raspberry Pi and curriculum retrieval on Android.
overview.zh: 本次演讲探讨在严格内存与模型规模限制下完成端侧智能体知识工作的系统方法，结合缓存增强生成、递归语言模型和有依据的评测，并展示树莓派法律分析与 Android 课程检索等案例。

talks.originalTitle: Which operating system is best for agentic mobile devices?

title.en: Which Operating System Is Best for Agentic Mobile Devices?
title.zh: 哪种操作系统最适合智能体移动设备？

talks.originalAbstract:
As AI-centred mobile devices diverge from smart phones we have the opportunity to reconsider which operating system to use. Android has a clear advantage right now because it has wide hardware support, but in a world that is less reliant on apps, Android has a lot of unnecessary baggage.

In this talk I look look at alternative operating systems, some of which have been around for a long time and are surprisingly mature. Among them are: Sailfish OS, which can trace a lineage back to the Linux-based phones from Nokia; Ubuntu Touch, which is a community project that carries on the work started by Canonical; and postMarketOS, which is a completely community-driven mobile OS. Or maybe something entirely new, but drawing on the vast expertise that rests in these projects. Running through each of these is a strong basis in Open Source components, which means that there is no lock-in to a single contributor (as with Android), and maximises shared value.

There are many options. Come along to find out what they are and the tradeoffs of each one.

overview.en: The talk explores alternative operating systems for agentic mobile devices, highlighting Sailfish OS, Ubuntu Touch, and postMarketOS, all rooted in open-source principles. These systems offer flexibility and avoid vendor lock-in, contrasting with Android's current dominance but unnecessary complexity. The discussion aims to identify the best fit for future AI-centric mobile devices.
overview.zh: 当以 AI 为中心的移动设备逐渐区别于智能手机，我们有机会重新考虑操作系统的选择。本次演讲将比较 Sailfish OS、Ubuntu Touch 和 postmarketOS 等成熟的替代方案；它们建立在开源组件之上，可避免被单一贡献者锁定。演讲也会说明 Android 的硬件支持优势、面向应用的冗余负担，以及不同方案各自的权衡。

title.zh: 从部件到整机：端侧 AI 液冷算力设备的规模化落地路径

talks.slug: p-109-从部件到整机-端侧ai液冷算力设备的规模化落地路径

It covers integration, platform standardization, thermal efficiency, environmental adaptability, operational reliability, and real-world deployment scenarios.
overview.zh: 本次演讲探讨端侧 AI 液冷算力设备如何从部件级突破走向整机规模化，涵盖系统集成、平台化与标准化、散热效率、环境适应性、运维可靠性及实际应用场景。

talks.originalTitle: SpecArtisans：面向 AI 编程的可验证 Spec-Driven 开发范式

title.en: SpecArtisans: A Verifiable Spec-Driven Development Paradigm for AI Coding
title.zh: SpecArtisans：面向 AI 编程的可验证 Spec-Driven 开发范式

talks.originalAbstract:
随着大语言模型和 AI 编程智能体的快速发展，AI 正逐渐从代码补全工具演进为能够参与需求分析、软件设计、代码实现和测试验证的开发主体。然而，在 AI 深度参与软件开发的过程中，一个关键问题也愈发突出：如何保证 AI 在需求、设计和实现的不同阶段始终准确理解并遵循原始需求？自然语言需求具有表达灵活、使用门槛低等优势，但也天然存在歧义，并且缺乏有效的机器验证机制。当需求经过设计、任务分解并最终转化为代码时，AI 对需求的理解可能逐步发生偏移，最终产生“实现看似合理，却与原始需求不一致”的问题。
本次分享将介绍我们针对这一问题设计的 SpecArtisans。SpecArtisans 是一套面向 AI 软件开发的 Spec-Driven 解决方案，其核心思想是在自然语言需求与程序代码之间引入结构化、可验证的半形式化软件规约（Spec），并以 Spec 作为连接需求设计、实现设计与代码生成的统一语义载体，使需求能够在 AI 软件开发的不同阶段持续传递、追踪和验证。围绕这一理念，SpecArtisans 构建了从需求规约、软件设计、代码实现到一致性验证的端到端开发工作流，并将相关能力封装为可复用的 Skill，与 AI 编程智能体协同完成软件开发任务。通过 SpecArtisans，我们希望让 AI 编程从“根据自然语言生成代码”进一步走向“基于明确、可追踪、可验证的需求完成软件开发”，探索更加可靠的 AI 原生软件工程开发范式。

overview.en: SpecArtisans is a Spec-Driven development paradigm for AI programming, aiming to ensure AI accurately follows original requirements throughout the software development process. It introduces structured, verifiable software specifications between natural language requirements and code, enabling consistent tracking and validation across design, implementation, and testing. By integrating these specifications into an end-to-end workflow, SpecArtisans enhances the reliability of AI-native software engineering.
overview.zh: SpecArtisans 是一种面向 AI 编程的 Spec-Driven 开发范式，旨在确保 AI 在软件开发各阶段准确遵循原始需求。它在自然语言需求与代码之间引入结构化、可验证的软件规约，实现需求在设计、实现和测试中的持续传递与验证。通过构建端到端的工作流并封装为可复用的 Skill，SpecArtisans 推动 AI 编程从生成代码向基于明确、可追踪、可验证需求的软件开发演进。

talks.originalTitle: Agentic AI as a Contributor to Mobile Linux

title.en: Agentic AI as a Contributor to Mobile Linux
title.zh: 智能体 AI 如何为移动 Linux 作出贡献

talks.originalAbstract:
Mobile Linux is a community-driven ecosystem, but contributing to it can sometimes mean finding your way through a large and complicated stack. From the kernel and hardware support to system services and applications, there is a lot to learn before even a small idea can turn into a working contribution.

Agentic AI is starting to make that journey easier. It can help contributors understand unfamiliar code, find their way around different parts of the system, debug problems, and turn ideas into working solutions. This can be especially valuable for people who want to contribute but may not have years of experience with every layer of Linux.

In this talk, I’ll share how agentic AI is already helping people contribute to mobile Linux today, and explore how these tools could make open-source development more approachable, collaborative, and accessible to a much wider community.

overview.en: Agentic AI is helping simplify contributions to Mobile Linux by assisting with code understanding, navigation, debugging, and idea implementation. It makes open-source development more accessible, especially for newcomers. This talk explores how agentic AI is already supporting contributions and its potential to enhance collaboration in the Mobile Linux community.
overview.zh: Agentic AI 正在帮助简化对 Mobile Linux 的贡献，通过协助代码理解、系统导航、调试和实现想法，使开源开发更易上手。它特别对新手有帮助，使更多人能够参与。本次演讲将探讨 Agentic AI 如何支持当前的贡献，并探索其在增强 Mobile Linux 社区协作方面的潜力。

talks.originalTitle: Agentic in Game AI, did we get any far?

title.en: Agentic AI in Games: How Far Have We Come?
title.zh: 游戏 AI 中的智能体：我们究竟走了多远？

talks.originalAbstract: We will show some demo achieves our goal, and we will talk and share how this can be extended to build an environment sets for different models as RL env and dataset.

overview.en: We will demonstrate some demo achievements toward our goal and discuss how this can be extended to build environment sets for different models as reinforcement learning environments and datasets.
overview.zh: 我们将展示一些达成目标的演示成果，并讨论如何扩展以构建适用于不同模型的环境集，作为强化学习环境和数据集。

talks.originalTitle: Your Agent's History Is Infrastructure, Not Logs — Building a Queryable Evidence Layer over Coding Agent Sessions

title.en: Your Agent's History Is Infrastructure, Not Logs — Building a Queryable Evidence Layer over Coding Agent Sessions
title.zh: 智能体历史记录是基础设施，而非日志——为编程智能体会话构建可查询的证据层

talks.originalAbstract: Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code, Pi — every coding agent you run leaves thousands of lines of session history on your disk, scattered across directories in incompatible formats, forgotten the moment the session ends. Obelisk turns that scattered history into open infrastructure: a single local SQLite + FTS5 index that agents query by writing code, and humans browse through a desktop app — the same evidence layer serving both. This talk covers the design decisions that made it work: why a relational index beats RAG for session history (tool-call causality, subagent hierarchies, and workflow phases don't survive embedding), why the query interface is "write a small script" instead of a fixed API, and how progressive disclosure keeps agents productive over a multi-table schema. Then the interesting part — what grows on top once history is queryable: cross-session failure pattern analysis, an explicit memory layer with human-approved write boundaries, usage analytics, and automated recap generation. Live demos throughout; the entire stack is open source and the multi-provider architecture is built for extension.

overview.en: Obelisk transforms scattered coding agent session histories into a unified, queryable infrastructure using SQLite and FTS5. It enables both agents and humans to interact with session data through code or a desktop app, supporting advanced features like failure analysis and memory management. The system is open source, with a multi-provider architecture designed for extension.
overview.zh: Obelisk 将分散的编程智能体会话历史转化为统一的可查询基础设施，使用 SQLite 和 FTS5 实现。它通过代码或桌面应用支持智能体和人类交互，具备故障分析、显式记忆层等高级功能。系统完全开源，采用多提供者架构，便于扩展。

talks.originalTitle: PenguinHarness：面向 1000+ 模型的高效自进化 Agent Harness

title.en: PenguinHarness: An Efficient Self-Evolving Agent Harness for 1,000+ Models
title.zh: PenguinHarness：面向 1000+ 模型的高效自进化 Agent Harness

talks.originalAbstract: PenguinHarness 是面向 AI 开发者的开源智能体自进化引擎，由 LlamaFactory（GitHub 7 万星）原班团队历时半年打造，支持 1000 多种本地与在线模型的统一接入与路由，最低仅需单 CPU 即可本地部署，满足企业级数据安全需求。该框架坚持最小化工具集与系统提示词的设计理念，让 Agent 能够自主完成模型训练、推理部署、模型评估、数据构建及 AI 应用开发等复杂任务，并通过内置的多智能体协作进化机制，让 Agent 在持续使用中越用越强。本次演讲将会分享我们在 Agent 自进化方向的探索与实践：如何用一句话在几分钟内生成接近生产可用的完整 AI 应用，如何借助开源的 PenguinHarness Skills 搭建从数据、评估到 Harness 自动迭代的完整进化 Loop，以及我们发布的 GDPevo Benchmark——首个在具有经济价值（GDP）的任务上评估 Agent 自进化能力的基准，实验表明自进化 Agent 在归纳学习后平均准确率提升 18.8%，Token 成本平均节省 7.5%。

overview.en: PenguinHarness is an open-source self-evolving agent framework developed by the LlamaFactory team, supporting over 1,000 models with minimal hardware requirements. It enables agents to autonomously perform training, deployment, evaluation, and application development through a minimal toolset and multi-agent collaboration. The talk will present how to rapidly build production-ready AI applications and evaluate self-evolving agents using the GDPevo Benchmark, showing an 18.8% accuracy improvement and 7.5% cost reduction.
overview.zh: PenguinHarness 是由 LlamaFactory 团队开发的开源自进化智能体框架，支持 1000 多种模型，仅需单 CPU 即可部署。它通过最小工具集和多智能体协作机制，使智能体能自主完成训练、部署、评估等任务。本次演讲将介绍如何快速构建生产级 AI 应用，并通过 GDPevo Benchmark 评估自进化能力，实验显示准确率提升 18.8%，Token 成本降低 7.5%。

talks.originalTitle: MemOS：Agent 自主进化的下一代记忆系统

title.en: MemOS 2.0: Key Technical Challenges and the Evolution of Memory Systems
title.zh: MemOS 2.0：记忆系统关键技术挑战与演进

talks.originalAbstract:
随着大模型从一次性问答走向持续交互、复杂任务执行与多智能体协作，记忆正在从外挂能力演变为 Agent 长期运行和持续进化的基础设施。MemOS 1.0—2.0 以多种记忆的统一管理和运行态治理为基础，完成了从记忆条目到用户、Agent、任务与 Session 状态的系统演进。
本次分享将重点讨论记忆如何推动 Agent 成长：MSCE 将执行轨迹逐层沉淀为可验证技能，PHASE-Tree 让角色状态在长期交互中保持身份稳定并持续变化；进一步结合以 Metis 为代表的记忆原生模型，探索如何让高频记忆状态和记忆操作参与模型前向。由此讨论下一代记忆系统的统一形态：记忆原生模型负责高密度、低延迟的模型内执行，外置记忆系统负责长期记忆、证据链、技能与角色状态的版本化治理，二者通过统一调度实现准入、同步、冲突处理、回退与重建。

overview.en: MemOS 2.0 addresses the evolution of memory systems from static management to runtime state control, focusing on long-term state maintenance, dynamic scheduling, and memory governance. It introduces runtime memory management, versioning, native models, and a foundational memory model, with applications in agent, companion, and enterprise services.
overview.zh: MemOS 2.0 从静态记忆管理升级为运行时状态管理，强调长期状态维护、动态调度与记忆治理。它引入运行态记忆管理、记忆版本化、原生模型及 Memory 基础模型底座，并结合 Agent、陪伴及企业服务等场景探讨下一代记忆系统的技术路径与落地机会。

talks.originalTitle: Building Self-Improving and Long-Horizon Agents

title.en: Building Self-Improving and Long-Horizon Agents
title.zh: 构建可自我改进的长时程智能体

talks.originalAbstract: The rapid advancement of large language models has enabled powerful AI agents with reasoning, planning, and coding capabilities. However, agent behavior is shaped not only by the base model, but also by its harness—the surrounding system that mediates the model’s interaction with the environment. In this talk, we will present our recent explorations of agent harness. First, we will introduce Self Harness, a new paradigm in which an LLM agent acts as its own harness engineer, autonomously improving the harness that supports its operation. Second, we will present Harness of Harness, exploring how to scale autonomous software development from hours to days while enabling continuous improvement. Finally, we will briefly share our recent explorations of agent harness for theoretical computer science, investigating how harness-based approaches can enable new forms of AI-assisted research and discovery.

overview.en: Building Self-Improving and Long-Horizon Agents explores how large language models can autonomously enhance their operational systems. The talk introduces Self Harness, where an LLM acts as its own harness engineer, and Harness of Harness, enabling continuous improvement over extended periods. It also touches on applying these methods to theoretical computer science for AI-assisted research.
overview.zh: 本次演讲探讨了如何让大语言模型自主提升其运行系统。演讲介绍了Self Harness，即让LLM充当自身系统工程师，并展示了Harness of Harness，实现长时间持续改进。此外，还简要分享了在理论计算机科学中应用这些方法进行AI辅助研究的探索。

talks.originalTitle: From Coding Agents to Autonomous Contributors: Designing the Operating Model for Agentic Software Engineering

title.en: From Coding Agents to Autonomous Contributors: Designing the Operating Model for Agentic Software Engineering
title.zh: 从编程智能体到自主贡献者：为智能体软件工程设计运行模式

talks.originalAbstract:
Coding agents can already write code. The harder problem is turning them into trustworthy contributors to a real software engineering lifecycle for production code.

As coding agents became increasingly common across our engineering organization, we began exploring what would happen if agents moved beyond assisting individual engineers and started contributing autonomously to software development workflows. Rather than defining an autonomous engineering framework upfront, I treated this as an engineering research problem: build real workflows, run them in CI, observe where they fail, and let those failures shape the architecture.

This talk shares that journey - from autonomous repository audits and organization-wide analysis to an autonomous Review → Auto-fix → Review loop.

Along the way, several architectural lessons emerged. Deterministic execution and probabilistic reasoning need different boundaries. Generation and verification should be separate responsibilities. Autonomous workflows need explicit safety boundaries, failure modes, and human escape hatches.

But the most difficult problem turned out to be neither model capability nor code generation:

How does an autonomous engineering system know when it is finished?

A reviewer can almost always find another possible improvement. Simply increasing the agent's turn budget or capping the number of iterations does not answer whether another iteration creates meaningful engineering value.

I'll share the architecture, experiments, failures, and practical design decisions behind these workflows—and explore why the next frontier of agentic software engineering may be less about making agents smarter and more about designing systems that know when to continue, when to stop, and when to converge and hand control back to a human.

overview.en: This talk examines how coding agents can move beyond individual assistance and become trustworthy contributors to production software workflows. It shares lessons from CI-based experiments, including separating generation from verification, setting safety boundaries, and deciding when an autonomous system should stop and return control to a human.
overview.zh: 本次演讲探讨编程智能体如何从个人辅助工具转变为生产级软件流程中可信赖的自主贡献者。内容涵盖生成与验证的职责分离、安全边界，以及自主系统何时应停止并把控制权交还给人类。

talks.originalTitle: Effective and high performance human-agent interaction

title.en: Effective and High-Performance Human–Agent Interaction
title.zh: 高效、高性能的人机智能体交互

talks.originalAbstract:
Current human-agent interfaces behave a lot like traditional chat or terminal interfaces, making them inefficient, insecure by default, and hard to use for humans. 

Taking the example of uni03C0, a Mac OS client to to the Pi coding agent, we look at how performance and security problems can be solved in a simple and effective way, turning a coding agent into a secure and high-precision tool for the human operating it.

overview.en: Using uni03C0, a macOS client for the Pi coding agent, this talk explores how human–agent interfaces can move beyond chat and terminal conventions. It focuses on practical ways to improve interaction performance, precision, usability, and security.
overview.zh: 本次演讲以 Pi 编程智能体的 macOS 客户端 uni03C0 为例，探讨人机智能体界面如何突破传统聊天框和终端模式，并通过实际设计提升交互效率、精确度、易用性与安全性。

talks.originalTitle: Agent First, Workflow Later：DeerFlow 的企业级智能体实践

title.en: Agent First, Workflow Later: Enterprise Agent Practices with DeerFlow
title.zh: Agent First, Workflow Later：DeerFlow 的企业级智能体实践

talks.originalAbstract:
企业业务持续变化，新的业务流程往往需要在多轮尝试中逐渐沉淀。如果一开始就将其写成固定 Workflow，不仅需要预先穷举大量分支，也会带来较高的开发和维护成本；但如果完全交给 Agent 自主执行，又必须面对权限、安全、可靠性和 Token 成本等企业级约束。
本次分享将结合 DeerFlow 在数家头部企业中的实践，介绍如何构建面向企业业务的 Super Agent 运行环境：通过 Skill 抽象可复用的业务能力，借助 MCP 和 CLI 对接内部 IT 系统，通过 IM 网关贯通用户身份与权限，并在关键操作中引入人工确认。
分享还将讨论一种正在探索的演进模式：让 Agent 在业务早期围绕目标尝试不同执行路径，记录计划、Skill 调用、关键状态和人工反馈；当成功轨迹逐渐稳定后，再将其沉淀为经过人工审核的 Workflow 和测试资产，在探索能力、执行可靠性与成本之间取得平衡。

overview.en: Drawing on DeerFlow deployments in large enterprises, this talk explains how to build a Super Agent environment with reusable skills, MCP and CLI integrations, identity-aware IM gateways, and human confirmation for critical actions. It also explores how successful agent trajectories can later become reviewed workflows and test assets.
overview.zh: 本次演讲结合 DeerFlow 在大型企业中的实践，介绍如何通过可复用 Skill、MCP 与 CLI 集成、贯通身份权限的 IM 网关及关键操作人工确认，构建企业级 Super Agent 环境，并将稳定的成功轨迹沉淀为经审核的工作流和测试资产。

talks.originalTitle: An Autonomous Runtime Shielding Agent for Linux Kernel Vulnerabilities

title.en: An Autonomous Runtime Shielding Agent for Linux Kernel Vulnerabilities
title.zh: 面向 Linux 内核漏洞的自主运行时防护智能体

talks.originalAbstract: We present a technical exploration of using an agent for emergency defense against kernel vulnerabilities. Once a vulnerability goes public, the official fix takes time to land, leaving the system exposed. Existing quick defenses key on one observed failure, so attackers slip past with a different trigger, and LLMs make such evasion cheap. Our autonomous agent reproduces the bug, reasons about its root cause, generates an eBPF hot shield, then turns attacker to strike its own shield and ships only what holds. The process is non-intrusive and hot-deployed, with no downtime and no source changes.

overview.en: This talk presents an autonomous agent for emergency defense against newly disclosed Linux kernel vulnerabilities. The agent reproduces a flaw, reasons about its root cause, generates an eBPF hot shield, actively tests that defense against evasive triggers, and deploys only validated protection without downtime or source changes.
overview.zh: 本次演讲介绍一种面向新披露 Linux 内核漏洞的自主应急防护智能体。它能够复现漏洞、分析根因、生成 eBPF 热防护，并主动使用不同触发方式验证防护效果，最终在无需停机或修改源代码的情况下部署通过验证的运行时保护。

talks.originalTitle: 开发者的AI造物：技术社区视角下的AI硬件共建之路

title.en: AI Creations for Developers: Co-Building AI Hardware from a Technical Community Perspective
title.zh: 开发者的 AI 造物：技术社区视角下的 AI 硬件共建之路

talks.originalAbstract:
AI正从云端走向端侧，从软件算法走向物理实体。在这一浪潮中，技术社区正成为AI硬件创新的核心驱动力——当大模型能力与开源硬件的开放性相遇，每一个开发者都有机会成为“AI造物主”。
立创开源硬件平台作为国内最大的硬件开源社区之一，月活用户超80万，开源项目逾10万。平台以“开源社区+EDA工具+供应链智造”的闭环模式，正在构建一条从AI创意到硬件实物的加速通道。本主题将从技术社区的视角，分享立创开源平台在AI硬件共建中的实践与思考——如何让AI能力“长”在硬件上，如何让开源协作加速AI硬件从0到1的落地。

overview.en: AI is moving from the cloud to edge devices and from software to physical entities. The technical community is becoming a key driver of AI hardware innovation, enabling developers to become "AI creators" through the combination of large models and open-source hardware. The LiChuang open hardware platform, with over 800,000 monthly active users and more than 100,000 open-source projects, is building a path to turn AI ideas into physical hardware through its closed-loop model of open community, EDA tools, and supply chain manufacturing.
overview.zh: AI正从云端走向端侧，从软件算法走向物理实体。技术社区正成为AI硬件创新的核心驱动力，使每个开发者都有机会成为“AI造物主”。立创开源硬件平台作为国内最大的硬件开源社区之一，拥有超80万月活用户和逾10万开源项目，通过“开源社区+EDA工具+供应链智造”的闭环模式，加速AI创意向硬件实物的转化。

talks.originalTitle: 从设备联网到设备协作：EMQ Device Agent 构建 A2A 分布式智能硬件网络

title.en: From Device Connectivity to Device Collaboration: Building an A2A Distributed Intelligent Hardware Network with EMQ Device Agent
title.zh: 从设备联网到设备协作：EMQ Device Agent 构建 A2A 分布式智能硬件网络

talks.originalAbstract: 过去十年，物联网解决了设备"连得上"的问题，但跨品牌、跨协议的设备仍难以围绕动态目标自主协作——传统方案依赖点对点 API 和硬编码规则，集成成本随设备规模快速上升。本演讲介绍如何使用 EMQ Device Agent 将物理设备抽象为具备命令、属性、事件语义模型的 AI 智能体，并基于 MQTT 与 A2A 协议构建可发现、可调用、可协作的分布式智能硬件网络。演讲将拆解设备语义建模、智能体运行时、A2A 服务发现与任务编排等关键技术，结合智能硬件、工业生产、能源管理、医疗设备辅助等场景，探讨从"单品智能"走向"系统智能"的工程路径。

overview.en: The talk discusses how EMQ Device Agent transforms physical devices into AI agents with command, property, and event semantics, enabling cross-brand, cross-protocol device collaboration through MQTT and A2A protocols. It explores key technologies like semantic modeling, agent runtime, and A2A service discovery, focusing on building a distributed intelligent hardware network for applications in smart hardware, industrial production, energy management, and medical devices.
overview.zh: 本次演讲介绍如何利用EMQ Device Agent将物理设备抽象为具备命令、属性和事件语义的AI 智能体，通过MQTT与A2A协议构建可发现、可调用、可协作的分布式智能硬件网络。演讲将解析设备语义建模、智能体运行时、A2A服务发现与任务编排等关键技术，并结合智能硬件、工业生产、能源管理、医疗设备辅助等场景，探讨从“单品智能”向“系统智能”的工程路径。

talks.originalTitle: From Connecting to Thinking: TuyaOpen's Agent-First OS for the Physical AI Era

title.en: From Connecting to Thinking: TuyaOpen's Agent-First OS for the Physical AI Era
title.zh: 从连接到思考：面向物理 AI 时代的 TuyaOpen 智能体优先操作系统

talks.originalAbstract: For the past decade, the IoT industry has been obsessed with one question: "How do we connect more devices?" Billions of endpoints came online, but the vast majority remain dumb data collectors — they sense, they transmit, but they never think.The Agentic AI era changes everything. In this talk, we introduce TuyaOpen — an open-source A-IoT operating system purpose-built for the Physical AI era, where devices evolve from passive connectors into autonomous, perceiving, reasoning, and acting agents. TuyaOpen pioneered the Agent-First design philosophy, embedding AI agent development as the core capability of the platform rather than bolting it on as an afterthought. At its heart lies a native multi-modal AI component stack (ai_components) covering audio, vision, text, and sensor modalities — the first of its kind in the A-IoT open-source ecosystem. Through a standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP) implementation on resource-constrained embedded devices, TuyaOpen enables Large Language Models to safely discover and control physical hardware — a capability previously limited to server-side applications.We will walk through the architecture that makes this possible: a unified Hardware Abstraction Layer spanning 9 chip platforms (from $2 MCUs to Linux SoCs), a three-tier edge-cloud-device inference model that balances latency, cost, and privacy, and TClaw — our device-side agent deployment framework that runs a full ReAct agent loop on a $5 Tuya T5 WIFI MCU. We'll also showcase the TuyaOpen IDE, the world's first AI-Native embedded development environment, which introduces a "Vibe Coding" paradigm — enabling developers to go from natural language prompt to compiled, flashed, and cloud-connected firmware in under 30 minutes.But architecture without proof is just theory. We'll demonstrate real commercial products developer stories and real use cases. Today on TuyaOpen: AI-powered fridge notes, 3D printers with cloud vision inspection, family companion robots, and children's smart seats — each built by different teams, each reaching mass production, all sharing the same Agent-First OS.The future of IoT is not just connected. It's thinking. Join us to see how TuyaOpen is making it happen — openly.

overview.en: TuyaOpen introduces an open-source A-IoT operating system designed for the Physical AI era, shifting from device connectivity to autonomous, thinking agents. It features a native multi-modal AI stack and a standardized Model Context Protocol, enabling LLMs to control hardware on embedded devices. The system supports a unified hardware abstraction layer, edge-cloud-device inference, and TClaw for running ReAct agent loops on low-cost MCUs, with real-world applications like AI fridges and companion robots already in mass production.
overview.zh: TuyaOpen 是一个专为物理 AI 时代设计的开源 A-IoT 操作系统，从设备连接转向自主思考的智能体。它包含原生多模态 AI 栈和标准化的模型上下文协议，使大语言模型能够控制嵌入式硬件。系统支持统一的硬件抽象层、边缘-云-设备推理模型以及 TClaw 框架，可在低成本 MCU 上运行 ReAct 智能体循环，已有 AI 冰箱、3D 打印机等实际产品投入量产。

talks.originalTitle: Building AI Agent Devices on RISC-V with DC-ROMA Mainboard III

title.en: Building AI Agent Devices on RISC-V with DC-ROMA Mainboard III
title.zh: 使用 DC-ROMA Mainboard III 在 RISC-V 上构建 AI 智能体设备

talks.originalAbstract:
As AI agents move from cloud-based services toward local and edge devices, the hardware platforms behind them are becoming increasingly important. RISC-V, with its open and extensible architecture, offers a new foundation for developers building and experimenting with AI-enabled devices.

This session introduces the DC-ROMA RISC-V Mainboard III for Framework Laptop 13, powered by the SpacemiT K3 AI SoC with RVA23 support. We will explore how a modular RISC-V platform can serve as a developer-ready environment for local AI and AI agent development.

The session will focus on the role of RISC-V devices in the emerging AI agent ecosystem, including local AI inference, agent application development, and the integration of AI capabilities into personal and edge computing devices. We will also discuss how CPU, AI acceleration, memory, and open-source software work together to create a practical platform for developers experimenting with AI agents on RISC-V.

overview.en: The talk discusses the use of RISC-V architecture in building AI agent devices, focusing on the DC-ROMA Mainboard III powered by SpacemiT K3 AI SoC. It explores how modular RISC-V platforms enable local AI and agent development, emphasizing the integration of AI capabilities into edge computing devices.
overview.zh: 本次演讲探讨了如何利用RISC-V架构构建AI 智能体设备，重点介绍了由SpacemiT K3 AI SoC驱动的DC-ROMA Mainboard III。演讲还探讨了模块化RISC-V平台如何支持本地AI和智能体开发，并强调了AI能力在边缘计算设备中的集成。
