talks.originalTitle: You Built the Prototype. Should It Become a Product?

title.en: You Built the Prototype. Should It Become a Product?
title.zh: 原型已经完成，它应该成为产品吗？

talks.originalAbstract:
A model, a board, and a working prototype can come together extremely quickly. The harder question is: how do you know whether that prototype should become a product?

This talk offers a practical product framework for evaluating AI-native hardware ideas before teams over-invest in building them. I’ll explore how to work backward from the user experience: What interaction is valuable enough to justify a new physical product? And what is the simplest combination of hardware, edge intelligence, and cloud capability needed to deliver it?

Using examples from AI toys, companions, wearables, and other emerging devices, we’ll look at the decisions that separate an impressive demo from something people will actually want, use, and pay for.

Key Takeaways
How to distinguish an AI hardware demo from the beginnings of a viable product
How to start with the user interaction and work backward into hardware and AI requirements
Which product decisions should be made before committing to a hardware architecture
How latency, power, connectivity, cloud cost, privacy, and form factor affect the product experience, not just the engineering
Common ways AI-native physical products become overbuilt, unreliable, or expensive before reaching users
A practical framework for deciding what a physical AI product actually needs in order to ship

overview.en: This talk offers a practical framework for deciding whether an AI-native hardware prototype should become a product. It works backward from user value to hardware and AI requirements, covering latency, power, connectivity, cloud cost, privacy, form factor, and common causes of overbuilt products.
overview.zh: 本次演讲提供一套实用框架，帮助团队判断 AI 原生硬件原型是否值得产品化。内容从用户价值反推硬件与 AI 需求，并讨论延迟、功耗、连接、云成本、隐私、形态以及产品过度设计等关键问题。

talks.originalTitle: AI 原生嵌入式产品研发：重塑软硬件研发范式

title.en: AI-Native Embedded Product Development: Reshaping the Hardware–Software R&D Paradigm
title.zh: AI 原生嵌入式产品研发：重塑软硬件研发范式

talks.slug: p-86-ai-原生嵌入式产品研发-重塑软硬件研发范式
talks.originalAbstract:
本次演讲将分享我们在 AI 原生嵌入式产品研发中的实践与探索：如何围绕 AI 重新组织软件、硬件、工具与验证流程，让 AI 从代码辅助逐步进入产品研发的主循环。
    演讲将从模块化架构与 Rust 嵌入式开发讲起，介绍如何通过清晰的模块边界和严格的编译检查，将更多问题左移到设计与编译阶段；再通过工程文档与上下文组织，以及面向 AI 的串口、调试器和示波器等周边调试能力，让真实设备变得可操作、可观察、可验证。研发 Harness 进一步管理任务状态、工具调用和验证证据，使 AI 能够在明确的目标与工程边界内自主完成实现、调试和多轮验证。目前，这套方法已经应用于实际产品研发，并正延伸到 PCB 与完整的软硬件闭环。
    演讲还将分享企业落地中的阶段性心得：如何先在资料和生态丰富的平台上快速验证产品，将成熟能力沉淀为可复用 Core，再迁移到面向成本、功耗和供应链的量产平台；以及在模型能力快速变化时，如何持续识别 AI 的能力边界，建立真正适合自身产品和团队的研发方式。

overview.en: This session shares an AI-native approach to embedded product development that reorganizes software, hardware, tooling, and validation around AI. It covers modular Rust architecture, AI-operable debugging tools, evidence-based development harnesses, and a path from rapid prototyping to cost- and power-conscious production platforms.
overview.zh: 本次演讲分享围绕 AI 重新组织软件、硬件、工具与验证流程的嵌入式产品研发实践。内容涵盖模块化 Rust 架构、面向 AI 的设备调试能力、基于验证证据的研发 Harness，以及从快速验证平台向量产平台迁移的方法。

talks.originalTitle: 从“可穿戴”到“懂你”：AI 智能体设备的产品化与场景落地

title.en: From Wearable to Understanding You: Productizing AI Agent Devices for Real-World Scenarios
title.zh: 从“可穿戴”到“懂你”：AI 智能体设备的产品化与场景落地

talks.slug: p-104-从-可穿戴-到-懂你-ai-智能体设备的产品化与场景落地
talks.originalAbstract:
AI Agent 正从软件走向可穿戴设备，但真正的产品突破，不只是把 AI 装进硬件，而是让设备能够持续感知用户状态，并提供个性化服务。本次分享将结合心境科技在脑机接口与 AI 可穿戴设备的产品实践，从用户需求、产品定义、场景设计到商业落地，探讨“感知—理解—服务”的智能体设备如何从技术能力转化为真实用户价值。

AI agents are moving from software into wearable devices, but the real product breakthrough is not simply putting AI into hardware—it is enabling devices to continuously sense user states and deliver personalized services. Drawing on MoodSense’s experience in BCI and AI wearables, this talk explores how agentic devices can turn sensing and intelligence into real user value through product design, scenario development, and commercialization.

overview.en: Drawing on product work in brain–computer interfaces and AI wearables, this talk explores how agentic devices can continuously sense user states and deliver personalized services. It follows the path from user needs and product definition through scenario design and commercialization.
overview.zh: 本次演讲结合脑机接口与 AI 可穿戴设备的产品实践，探讨智能体设备如何持续感知用户状态并提供个性化服务，覆盖用户需求、产品定义、场景设计与商业落地的完整路径。

talks.originalTitle: The World as the Interface: Building an Open Agent Ecosystem for AI Glasses

title.en: The World as the Interface: Building an Open Agent Ecosystem for AI Glasses
title.zh: 以世界为界面：构建面向 AI 眼镜的开放智能体生态

talks.originalAbstract:
AI glasses will not become the next computing platform by placing smartphone applications in front of the user’s eyes. Their deeper potential is to make the world itself the interface: turning vision, voice, environmental context, and device capabilities into a continuous loop of perception, understanding, coordination, action, and human confirmation.

This talk explores how an open agent ecosystem can enable that transition. Rather than depending on one model, assistant, or closed application platform, the ecosystem connects multimodal devices, AI agents, tools, interfaces, applications, developers, and services through an open coordination layer.

Drawing on more than a decade of building AI and AR products and working with developer communities across Asia, Europe, and North America, Weiqi Zhao will share a product and ecosystem framework for moving from isolated demonstrations to extensible, real-world agentic experiences.

Open protocols and projects, including Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent2Agent (A2A), Agent-to-User Interface (A2UI), OpenXR, OpenClaw, and selected third-party community projects, will illustrate how different ecosystem layers can work together. These projects can connect agents with device capabilities, coordinate independent agents, support adaptive interfaces, and enable portable spatial experiences.

A core goal of this ecosystem is to lower the barrier for agent developers in China and worldwide. Developers should be able to connect their agents with multimodal devices, adapt them to local market needs, and deploy them across industrial, educational, cultural, retail, accessibility, field-service, and personal-assistant scenarios.

The session will also address the realities of product deployment: latency, battery life, privacy, permissions, human attention, safety, developer experience, and the boundary between open-source innovation and commercial product engineering.

Attendees will leave with a practical framework for connecting devices, agents, open projects, developers, and vertical applications without depending on a single closed platform.

overview.en: This talk presents a product and ecosystem framework for turning the world into the interface for AI glasses. It connects multimodal devices, agents, tools, developers, and services through open protocols while addressing deployment realities such as latency, battery life, privacy, permissions, safety, and developer experience.
overview.zh: 本次演讲提出一套让现实世界成为 AI 眼镜交互界面的产品与生态框架，通过开放协议连接多模态设备、智能体、工具、开发者与服务，并讨论延迟、续航、隐私、权限、安全和开发体验等落地问题。

talks.originalTitle: openvela：从开源操作系统到 AI 硬件智能体的基础底座

title.en: openvela: From an Open-Source Operating System to the Foundation for AI Hardware Agents
title.zh: openvela：从开源操作系统到 AI 硬件智能体的基础底座

talks.originalTitle: Voice AI Is Entering Its Second Generation: Lessons from Enterprise Voice Agent Deployments

title.en: Voice AI Is Entering Its Second Generation: Lessons from Enterprise Voice Agent Deployments
title.zh: 语音 AI 正迈入第二代：企业级语音智能体部署经验

talks.originalAbstract: In this talk, I'll share six industry shifts that are redefining Voice AI—from intelligence to execution, from speech to conversation, from APIs to platforms, and ultimately from conversations to long-term relationships. While these patterns first emerged in enterprise deployments, they point toward the future of open-source AI infrastructure and consumer AI experiences.

overview.en: The talk discusses six key industry shifts transforming Voice AI, including moving from intelligence to execution and from APIs to platforms. These changes, initially seen in enterprise voice agent deployments, signal the future of open-source AI infrastructure and consumer AI experiences. The focus is on evolving Voice AI from short interactions to long-term relationships.

talks.originalTitle: Rethinking Residual Connections: Toward Depth-Effective Language Model Scaling

title.en: Rethinking Residual Connections: Toward Depth-Effective Language Model Scaling
title.zh: 重新思考残差连接：迈向深度有效的语言模型扩展

talks.originalAbstract: Increasing LLM depth does not necessarily translate into proportional gains in model capability. Under conventional residual architectures, deeper models can suffer from the Curse of Depth: residual-stream accumulation weakens the functional contribution of later layers, leaving a substantial fraction of added parameters underutilized. In this work, we systematically investigate whether recent residual-connection designs can overcome this limitation and enable depth-effective scaling. We benchmark a broad range of approaches—including Attention Residual, mHC, LayerNorm scaling, KEEL, and other residual-stream modifications—under controlled pre-training settings across model depths, parameter scales, and compute budgets. Beyond final validation loss, we evaluate layer utilization, representation evolution, gradient dynamics, effective depth, and downstream reasoning performance. Our results reveal substantial differences between methods that appear similar at small scale: while several designs improve optimization stability or shallow-model performance, only a subset sustains meaningful contributions from later layers as depth increases. These findings establish residual architecture as a critical scaling dimension alongside model width, data, and compute, and identify a promising route toward models that achieve stronger capabilities by scaling effective—rather than merely nominal—depth.

overview.en: Researchers explore whether recent residual-connection designs can enable effective depth scaling in language models. They evaluate various methods across different model depths and parameter scales, finding that only some designs sustain meaningful contributions from deeper layers. These results highlight residual architecture as a key factor in model scaling, alongside width, data, and compute.
overview.zh: 研究人员探讨近期残差连接设计是否能实现语言模型的有效深度扩展。他们在不同模型深度和参数规模下评估多种方法，发现只有部分设计能维持深层网络的有效贡献。这些结果强调残差架构是模型扩展的关键因素之一，与模型宽度、数据和计算资源并列。

talks.originalTitle: Scale-up Interconnect System for Supernodes

title.en: Scale-up Interconnect System for Supernodes
title.zh: 面向超级节点的 Scale-up 互联系统

talks.originalAbstract: The "brute-force miracle" of large models relies on the stacking of computational power, and supernodes serve as the physical carrier of that computational power. As model architectures evolve from Full Attention to Sparse/Linear Attention, the storage and transmission pressure of KV Cache is significantly reduced. However, the combination of tensor parallelism and sequence parallelism dramatically increases the demand for collective communication, necessitating collaborative computation-communication optimization and operator overlapping. At the interconnect level, architectural transitions from PCIe to NVLink, the different trade-offs between SUE and UALink in end-network division of labor, and the distinctions between message semantics and memory semantics, as well as between source-side ordering and destination-side ordering, collectively determine the performance ceiling of supernode Scale-up networks. Particularly during the decode phase, network bandwidth directly affects inference throughput. In the future, supernode interconnection will need to strike a balance among performance, cost, and ecosystem to better support the demands of both training and inference.

overview.en: The talk discusses the challenges and optimizations in scaling up interconnect systems for supernodes, focusing on how architectural transitions and communication strategies impact performance. As model architectures shift to sparse/linear attention, reducing KV Cache pressure, tensor and sequence parallelism increase collective communication demands. The interconnect system must balance performance, cost, and ecosystem to support both training and inference efficiently.
overview.zh: 本次演讲探讨了超节点互连系统扩展中的挑战与优化，重点分析了架构转变和通信策略对性能的影响。随着模型架构转向稀疏/线性注意力，KV缓存压力降低，但张量并行和序列并行显著增加了集体通信需求。互连系统需在性能、成本和生态系统间取得平衡，以高效支持训练和推理需求。

talks.originalTitle: 昇腾开源训练生态建设与演进

title.en: Building and Evolving the Ascend Open-Source Training Ecosystem
title.zh: 昇腾开源训练生态建设与演进

talks.originalAbstract: 作为算力厂商，积极拥抱开源社区，坚持对外开放是必须的选择，来满足客户的技术需求和规划。昇腾几年来在开源训练方向持续投入，正采用「自底向上、原生优先、插件增强」策略，积极拥抱第三方开源社区，并按分层、分场景的方式覆盖开发链路。本次分享中，我们将介绍昇腾如何通过底层技术兼容构建扎实的训练后端，如何参与社区建设和持续看护，并在社区基础适配之外额外贡献了如关键的性能、精度特性。

overview.en: As a computing power provider, embracing open-source communities and maintaining openness is essential to meet customer needs. Ascend has been continuously investing in open-source training, adopting a strategy of "bottom-up, native-first, plugin-enhancement" to actively engage with third-party communities. This talk will cover how Ascend builds a solid training backend through foundational technology compatibility, participates in community development, and contributes additional performance and accuracy features beyond standard compatibility.
overview.zh: 作为算力厂商，积极拥抱开源社区、坚持对外开放是满足客户需求的必然选择。昇腾多年来持续投入开源训练，采用“自底向上、原生优先、插件增强”策略，积极融入第三方开源社区。本次分享将介绍昇腾如何通过底层技术兼容构建扎实的训练后端，参与社区建设并持续维护，同时在社区基础适配之外贡献关键性能与精度特性。

talks.originalTitle: 面向开源模型的 AI-Ready 数据生产与动态数据训练

title.en: AI-Ready Data Production and Dynamic Data Training for Open-Source Models
title.zh: 面向开源模型的 AI-Ready 数据生产与动态数据训练

1. 范式迁移：模型效果越来越依赖高质量训练数据

3. Agentic Execution：Agent、Skills 与 Harness
4. 闭环进化：Eval-Driven Data Production
5. 工程实践：Data-Centric AI 开源生态落地与未来演进

It explores agentic execution through agents, skills, and harnesses, along with a closed-loop evolution driven by evaluation. The session also covers engineering practices for implementing a data-centric AI open ecosystem.

talks.originalTitle: SynthCommonCorpus: the largest open synthetic pretraining corpus built for agentic models

title.en: SynthCommonCorpus: The Largest Open Synthetic Pretraining Corpus Built for Agentic Models
title.zh: SynthCommonCorpus：面向智能体模型构建的最大开放合成预训练语料库

talks.originalAbstract:
SynthCommonCorpus (release autumn 2026) is the largest open synthetic pretraining corpus built for agentic models, and the first in which tool calls, multi-step decomposition and adversarial examples are part of the pretraining distribution. It exists to make one question askable: what does a model look like if it learned to act the way it learned syntax?
A web document is a finished artifact with the reasoning nonexistent - no decision path, no tool call, no failed attempt, no recovery from a bad result. Those traces were, as a rule, never written down anywhere. So every agentic model today is a document predictor that had agency grafted on in post-training, from a data pool orders of magnitude smaller than pretraining, which is a plausible explanation for why agentic competence stays brittle and concentrated in the largest models. 
Building it by crawling is not an option, and increasingly not an option for anything. Pretraining is already data-bound - Epoch AI puts exhaustion of the effective public text stock between 2026 and 2032, median 2028 - but the stock is not merely fixed, it is contracting, under content removals, licensing disputes and a broad hardening against AI scraping, while the legal ground beneath everything already crawled keeps moving. FineWeb, DCLM and Nemotron-CC are good answers to how you extract more from Common Crawl. They are answers on the wrong curve.
The technique that gets off that curve is settled practice and almost entirely private. MiniMax, Kimi, Nemotron and Phi all rely on synthetic generation; none of the resulting data is public. The open ecosystem is being locked out of the input that now determines capability, and the open–closed gap is quietly changing character - from a compute gap into a data-engineering gap. What public work exists is narrow: mostly rephrasing web text rather than generating new task structure, mostly English, and the largest efforts closed outright, with BeyondWeb generating a trillion tokens and releasing none of them.
The recipe has already been proven at small scale. SYNTH, the first open synthetic-only pretraining corpus - 80B tokens from 58,698 Wikipedia articles - collapses pre-, mid- and post-training into a single stage. Models trained on it undergo no SFT and no RLHF, and acquire reasoning, retrieval, instruction following and multilingual output as native capabilities of one run. At iso-compute it beats filtered web data, and the Baguettotron suite (56M to 13B/1B-active) tops factual precision in every parameter tier on 10–140× fewer training tokens. 
SynthCommonCorpus is that result scaled by two orders of magnitude, with every fact still traceable to a licensed seed - which makes it the first corpus at this scale whose knowledge content is enumerable, and so the first on which memorization and contamination can be measured rather than guessed at.
The talk covers how it is built and what we learnt along the way.

overview.en: The SynthCommonCorpus is the largest open synthetic pretraining corpus for agentic models, designed to explore how models learn to act like they learn syntax. It includes tool calls, multi-step reasoning, and adversarial examples, addressing limitations in current data sources. The corpus is built using synthetic generation, ensuring traceability and enabling measurable memorization and contamination.
overview.zh: SynthCommonCorpus 是目前最大的开源合成预训练语料库，专为具有自主行为能力的模型设计，包含工具调用、多步骤分解和对抗性示例，旨在探索模型如何像学习语法一样学习行动。该语料库通过合成生成构建，确保所有信息均可追溯，从而实现对记忆和污染的可测量分析。

talks.originalTitle: The Smol Training Handbook: One Tradeoff, Any Scale

title.en: The Smol Training Handbook: One Tradeoff, Any Scale
title.zh: Smol 训练手册：一个权衡，适用于任意规模

talks.originalAbstract:
Training state-of-the-art LLMs means solving the same problem at every scale: memory is fixed, compute is expensive, and you must trade off communication against computation under that constraint. This talk walks through the choices that problem forces, from optimizing a single GPU (activation recomputation, flash-attention, roofline profiling) to scaling across thousands (data, context, tensor, pipeline, and expert parallelism).
You'll see how each parallelism strategy makes the same memory-compute-communication tradeoff visible in different ways, why combining all five requires understanding your infrastructure, and which open-source frameworks and playbooks actually work in production.
The audience leaves knowing which parallelism strategy fits which constraint, how to profile for it with the roofline model, and why NCCL flags and infrastructure setup are not optional.

overview.en: Training state-of-the-art LLMs involves balancing memory, compute, and communication across different scales. The talk explores parallelism strategies like data, context, and pipeline parallelism, emphasizing the importance of infrastructure understanding and practical open-source tools. It concludes with guidance on selecting the right strategy and profiling techniques for production environments.
overview.zh: 训练最先进的LLM需要在不同规模下平衡内存、计算和通信。演讲探讨了数据、上下文和流水线并行等策略，强调了对基础设施的理解和实用开源工具的重要性。最后提供了选择合适策略和生产环境配置的指导。

talks.originalTitle: 机理合规审计与内生安全加固

title.en: Mechanism-Based Compliance Auditing and Intrinsic Security Hardening
title.zh: 机理合规审计与内生安全加固

talks.originalAbstract:
大语言模型的快速迭代不断拓宽人工智能的能力边界，但大模型缺失内生安全机理，已然成为其落地高风险场景、实现可信部署的核心瓶颈。当前主流人工智能安全与治理研究，大多聚焦模型输出层面开展外部约束与事后修正，无法从底层保障模型内在机理可靠性。与此同时，受神经元多义性固有难题制约，OpenAI、Anthropic等国际头部AI企业采用的机理解释技术，存在三大根本性缺陷：（1）机理语义边界缺乏严谨定义；（2）解释结果缺少数理完备性证明；（3）无法从机理维度拆解、解析模型整体性能。综上，现有可解释性体系尚不满足可追溯、可核验、可追责的机理审计与安全问责要求。
针对上述行业共性瓶颈，本教程关注的等效交互机理解释理论，系统性突破了传统解释方法的底层局限。本教程将结合多垂类大模型应用场景，详解该技术在模型安全审计、内生安全加固、模型训练效率优化等方向的核心应用，深度剖析大模型潜藏的隐性伦理风险与安全隐患，并进一步梳理可信大模型机理研究的发展逻辑与未来技术演进方向。
本次讲座核心内容如下：（1）严格证明神经网络复杂的决策逻辑，能够被精准解构为稀疏化交互机理；（2）构建大模型决策机理形式化审计方案，证实各类开源大模型均内嵌大量存在逻辑谬误的风险机理；（3）论证神经网络整体泛化能力，源于可泛化机理与不可泛化机理的协同作用，且两类机理分别服从特定的解析分布；（4）发现业界主流开源大模型存在交互机理表征趋同现象，实证相较于模型架构、训练数据，内在交互机理是决定前沿模型特性的第一性表征；（5）提出机理对齐训练范式，验证相较于传统输出导向监督训练，机理对齐训练可大幅提升大模型训练效率，同时加固模型内生机理安全。

overview.en: The talk examines intrinsic security risks in large language models and explains why output-level constraints cannot guarantee trustworthy behavior. It introduces the theory of equivalent interaction mechanism interpretation and its applications to formal mechanism auditing, intrinsic security hardening, and training-efficiency optimization. The session also covers findings on risky mechanisms in open-source models, model generalization, and mechanism-alignment training.
overview.zh: 本次讲座聚焦大语言模型的内生安全问题，提出等效交互机理解释理论，系统突破传统方法局限，为模型安全审计、内生安全加固及训练效率优化提供解决方案。内容涵盖神经网络决策逻辑解构、形式化审计方案构建、泛化能力分析及机理对齐训练范式验证。

talks.originalTitle: TransferQueue: An Asynchronous, High-Performance Streaming Data Engine for Post-Training

title.en: TransferQueue: An Asynchronous, High-Performance Streaming Data Engine for Post-Training
title.zh: TransferQueue：面向后训练的异步高性能流式数据引擎

talks.originalAbstract: Large model workflows are becoming increasingly complex. Take post-training as an example: it requires multiple computational tasks to collaborate, with intricate data dependencies between them. Existing industry solutions do not distinguish between data flow and control flow, which easily leads to imbalanced computational load and reduced resource utilization. To address this challenge, we propose—for the first time in the industry—an asynchronous streaming data engine with data-control separation. By splitting the transfer of monolithic data blocks into sample-level data streams, it supports data routing at arbitrary granularity and minimizes task blocking. Our core idea is simple: TransferQueue acts as a transit port for data, managing where the data should come from and where it should go. Building on TransferQueue, we put forward several technical positions to guide the design of future computing systems. First, from post-training to tool calling and further to multi-agent systems, the components involved in training and inference are proliferating, and their communication patterns are becoming increasingly complex. Both upper-level frameworks and lower-level collective communication rely on static orchestration, lacking the ability to schedule dynamically at runtime. We position TransferQueue as the communication middleware of large model computing systems, decoupling these computational processes so that tasks no longer need to be manually orchestrated, thereby achieving automatic pipelining and overlap. TransferQueue also provides a panoramic data scheduling capability, delivering both efficient communication and programming simplicity—a significant advantage over mainstream industry implementations.

overview.en: TransferQueue is an asynchronous, high-performance streaming data engine designed for post-training workflows. It separates data and control flow, enabling efficient data routing and minimizing task blocking. By acting as a transit port for data, TransferQueue supports dynamic scheduling and automatic pipelining in large model computing systems, offering improved resource utilization and communication efficiency.
overview.zh: TransferQueue 是一种异步、高性能的流数据引擎，专为后训练工作流设计。它分离数据与控制流，实现高效的数据路由并减少任务阻塞。通过作为数据中转站，TransferQueue 支持动态调度和自动流水线，在大模型计算系统中提升资源利用率和通信效率，相较于主流行业实现具有显著优势。

talks.originalTitle: C-to-Rust Code Translation: A Three-Stage Curriculum of Pretraining, Debugging-Aware SFT, and Task-Specific SFT

title.en: C-to-Rust Code Translation: A Three-Stage Curriculum of Pretraining, Debugging-Aware SFT, and Task-Specific SFT
title.zh: C 到 Rust 代码翻译：预训练、调试感知 SFT 与任务专用 SFT 的三阶段课程

talks.originalAbstract: Translating C code into safe, idiomatic Rust is a longstanding software-engineering goal because it can eliminate entire classes of memory-safety vulnerabilities while preserving the functional behavior of legacy systems. Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for this task but typically underperform when applied off-the-shelf, since general-purpose pretraining rarely emphasizes idiomatic Rust generation, cross-language semantic equivalence, or the ability to reason about and repair compiler/runtime feedback. In this report we describe a three-stage fine-tuning curriculum applied to Qwen3-27B that is designed to progressively specialize the model for the C-to-Rust (C2Rust) translation task: (1) continued pretraining on Rust-centric corpora to strengthen the model's prior over idiomatic Rust syntax and standard-library usage; (2) supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on the microsoft/Verus_Training_Data dataset to instill debugging and self-repair behavior over Rust code; and (3) task-specific SFT on paired C/Rust solutions derived from LeetCode problems to teach direct semantic translation. We evaluate the resulting model using the agentic, static-analysis-guided verification framework of SACTOR, which performs structure-aware, two-phase (unidiomatic to idiomatic) translation with foreign-function-interface (FFI)-based end-to-end (E2E) testing. We report success rate, idiomaticity (Clippy lint counts, unsafe-code fraction), and failure-mode analyses, and compare our fine-tuned model against baseline Qwen3-27B and other LLMs evaluated under the same framework.

overview.en: Translating C code into safe Rust is a key goal for improving software safety. This talk presents a three-stage training approach for Qwen3-27B, including Rust-focused pretraining, debugging-aware SFT, and task-specific SFT. The model is evaluated using SACTOR, showing improved success rates and idiomatic code quality compared to baselines.
overview.zh: 将 C 代码转换为安全、符合 Rust 习惯的代码，是提升软件安全性的重要目标。本次演讲介绍面向 Qwen3-27B 的三阶段训练方法，包括 Rust 专项预训练、调试感知的监督微调和任务特定微调。通过 SACTOR 框架评估，该模型在成功率和代码规范性方面优于基线模型。

talks.originalTitle: Applications of Voice Agents in Embodied Intelligence and High‑Quality Data‑Driven Solutions

title.en: Applications of Voice Agents in Embodied Intelligence and High-Quality Data-Driven Solutions
title.zh: 语音智能体在具身智能与高质量数据驱动解决方案中的应用

talks.originalAbstract:
Embodied intelligence has emerged as a key track for the physical deployment of AI. The industry is shifting from traditional software‑only conversational interaction to a new era of physical‑world integration of perception, decision‑making and execution. Competition among AI Agents is now heavily focused on real‑world deployment capabilities.
As the core human‑machine‑interaction carrier for embodied intelligence, Voice Agents are facing shared industrial challenges. Most products fail to make the paradigm shift from “being able to chat” to “being able to act”. Three major bottlenecks prevail: stiff and unnatural interactions, low accuracy in interpreting ambiguous spoken instructions, inefficient task execution in complex dynamic environments, and inadequate interaction‑safety frameworks. These issues severely limit large‑scale commercialization of embodied and edge‑AI terminals such as intelligent cockpits and home‑service robots.
Real‑world domain shift is the root cause of these pain points. Simulated lab‑generated data cannot replicate the complexity, dynamism and randomness of physical environments, resulting in poor post‑deployment adaptability and weak scene generalization for models. High‑quality, authentic and multi‑dimensional multimodal interaction data therefore becomes critical to breaking through bottlenecks in embodied Voice‑Agent interaction and enabling iterative product upgrades.
This presentation explores real‑world applications of Voice Agents in embodied intelligence. It dissects interaction pain points and corresponding data solutions for two flagship scenarios: intelligent cockpits and home‑service robots. It systematically outlines core standards and deployment logic for next‑generation embodied‑intelligence and edge‑AI interaction datasets. Drawing on Magic Data’s technical capabilities and service portfolio, the talk elaborates on key strengths including scenario‑specific data construction, full‑coverage dialect and multilingual support, and end‑to‑end compliance & safety. Targeting real‑world deployment hurdles, actionable data‑optimization strategies and scene‑adaptation frameworks are proposed to address core problems including unnatural interactions, inaccurate command comprehension and unsafe execution. The goal is to accelerate the transition of embodied‑intelligence Voice Agents from lab prototypes toward large‑scale, highly‑reliable and inclusive industrial roll‑out, and speed up intelligent upgrading across physical‑AI scenarios.

overview.en: This talk examines how high-quality real-world multimodal data can help voice agents progress from conversation to reliable action in embodied systems. It covers intelligent cockpits and home-service robots, with practical approaches to natural interaction, command understanding, safe execution, multilingual coverage, and compliant data construction.
overview.zh: 本次演讲探讨高质量真实世界多模态数据如何帮助语音智能体从“能对话”走向具身系统中的可靠行动。内容涵盖智能座舱和家庭服务机器人，并讨论自然交互、指令理解、安全执行、多语言覆盖及合规数据建设。

talks.originalTitle: Teaching AI to Improve AI: From Experimental Feedback to Meta-Evolution

title.en: Teaching AI to Improve AI: From Experimental Feedback to Meta-Evolution
title.zh: 教 AI 改进 AI：从实验反馈到元进化

talks.originalAbstract:
Large language models are evolving from coding assistants into research agents that can propose solutions, run experiments, interpret feedback, and iteratively improve their results. Yet achieving a higher score in a single experiment does not mean that a system has truly learned how to improve.
This talk explores how execution-grounded experimentation can be transformed into reusable improvement capabilities. We first introduce the minimal AI4AI loop—propose, execute, evaluate, and revise—and distinguish one-off optimization from self-evolution, where experience changes the system’s future behavior. Through representative success and failure cases from NatureBench, we examine the key bottlenecks facing scientific agents, including method selection, implementation depth, and compute allocation. We then present Frontis-MA1 and OpenMLE, showing how executable tasks, structured feedback, evolutionary search, and post-training can be connected within a unified learning loop.
Finally, we return to recursive self-improvement: what would it take for an improved AI improver to take over the next improvement cycle and continually produce stronger successors?

overview.en: Large language models are evolving from coding assistants to research agents capable of proposing solutions, running experiments, and iteratively improving results. This talk discusses how execution-based experimentation can be transformed into reusable improvement capabilities, using the AI4AI loop and case studies from NatureBench. It also explores the potential for recursive self-improvement in AI systems.
overview.zh: 大型语言模型正从代码助手演变为能够提出解决方案、运行实验并迭代改进结果的研究智能体。本次演讲探讨了如何将基于执行的实验转化为可复用的改进能力，介绍了AI4AI循环和NatureBench中的案例研究。最后，还探讨了AI系统实现递归自我改进的潜力。

talks.originalTitle: AMD ROCm and Radeon-Powered Real2Sim2Real Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

title.en: AMD ROCm and Radeon-Powered Real2Sim2Real Vision-Language-Action Manipulation
title.zh: AMD ROCm 与 Radeon 驱动的 Real2Sim2Real 视觉-语言-动作操控

talks.originalAbstract: This talk presents an end-to-end Real2Sim2Real embodied AI workflow built entirely on AMD ROCm and Radeon GPUs, spanning data generation, policy training, simulation validation, and real-world deployment. We begin by generating large-scale synthetic robot demonstrations in the Genesis physics simulator using GPU hardware rasterization, then convert them into the standard LeRobot dataset format. A SmolVLA-450M vision-language-action policy is fine-tuned entirely on the AMD platform using ROCm-native PyTorch. The trained policy is first validated through closed-loop evaluation in Genesis simulation, then deployed directly to a physical Franka robotic arm — completing a full real-to-sim-to-real loop that rigorously tests sim-to-real transfer and policy robustness.

overview.en: AMD ROCm and Radeon GPUs enable an end-to-end Real2Sim2Real workflow for embodied AI, covering data generation, policy training, simulation validation, and real-world deployment. Synthetic robot demonstrations are generated using GPU hardware rasterization and converted to LeRobot format. A SmolVLA-450M policy is fine-tuned on AMD hardware, validated in simulation, and deployed on a Franka robotic arm, demonstrating effective sim-to-real transfer and policy robustness.
overview.zh: AMD ROCm 和 Radeon GPU 实现了端到端的 Real2Sim2Real 具身智能工作流，涵盖数据生成、策略训练、仿真验证和实际部署。该工作流利用 GPU 硬件光栅化生成大规模合成机器人演示，并转换为 LeRobot 格式；SmolVLA-450M 策略则在 AMD 硬件上微调，经仿真验证后部署到 Franka 机械臂，展示仿真到现实迁移与策略鲁棒性。

talks.originalTitle: Nexus: a new cross-platform GPU-based Rust multiphysics simulator for robotics and training datasets generation

title.en: Nexus: A New Cross-Platform GPU-Based Rust Multiphysics Simulator for Robotics and Training Dataset Generation
title.zh: Nexus：面向机器人与训练数据生成的全新跨平台 GPU Rust 多物理场模拟器

talks.originalAbstract: With the emergence of World Models for robotics and training datasets generation, high-performance multiphysics simulators are becoming central to robotics and model training with frameworks like Newton (Nvidia Warp, Python) and Genesis (Taichi, Python). In this talk, we are introducing the project Nexus: a new alternative written in Rust (compiled with rust-gpu), and running on all GPU platforms, including the web.

overview.en: Nexus is a new cross-platform GPU-based Rust multiphysics simulator designed for robotics and training datasets generation. talks.originalTitle: From Single-Robot Intelligence to Multi-Agent Coordination: The Evolution of AIRSEAI

title.en: From Single-Robot Intelligence to Multi-Agent Coordination: The Evolution of AIRSEAI
title.zh: 从单机器人智能到多智能体协同：AIRSEAI 的演进

talks.originalAbstract: As embodied AI evolves from single-robot operation to multi-agent coordination, system challenges expand from perception, planning, and control to data lifecycles, task coordination, state sharing, and adaptation under communication and resource constraints. This talk presents the evolution of AIRSEAI, an open-source embodied AI infrastructure developed by AIRS. AIRSEAI 1.0 establishes a modular mobile manipulation pipeline with task planning, navigation, execution feedback, replanning, and simulation-to-real integration. AIRSEAI 2.0 extends this foundation through the OPENARMS dual-arm platform, multimodal sensing, pluggable model tools, capability evaluation, and a standardized workflow covering data collection, training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and deployment. AIRSEAI 3.0 further supports multi-agent task coordination, state sharing, edge–cloud collaboration, and constrained decision-making under dynamic and communication-impaired conditions. The talk will also discuss practical trade-offs and open challenges in heterogeneous interoperability, scalable simulation, safety-constrained coordination, and real-world multi-robot deployment.

overview.en: The talk discusses the evolution of AIRSEAI from single-robot intelligence to multi-agent coordination, highlighting its modular pipeline, multimodal sensing, and support for multi-agent task coordination and constrained decision-making. It also addresses challenges in interoperability, simulation, and real-world deployment.
overview.zh: 本次演讲探讨了AIRSEAI从单机器人智能向多智能体协作的演进，重点介绍了其模块化管道、多模态感知以及支持多智能体任务协调和受限决策的能力。还讨论了异构互操作性、仿真和实际部署中的挑战。

talks.originalTitle: Train it or code it? Let the robot decide

title.en: Train It or Code It? Let the Robot Decide
title.zh: 训练还是编程？让机器人自己决定

talks.originalAbstract:
At GOSIM Paris in May, I presented Skill Foundry: an embodied learning loop in which an AI coding agent can operate across robot software, training, execution, multimodal observation, memory, and a growing library of reusable skills.

In the months since, the field has started converging rapidly toward pieces of the same direction. NVIDIA GEAR, the embodied-AI research group behind projects such as GR00T, Eureka and Voyager, introduced ASPIRE, combining multimodal execution diagnosis, autonomous program repair and a continually expanding robot skill library. The NVIDIA/CMU/Berkeley team behind ENPIRE pushed coding agents into autonomous real-world policy improvement. In parallel, RHO introduced Robotics Harness Optimization, where coding agents evolve entire multi-file robot policy repositories from execution and reward feedback.

These are no longer isolated demonstrations of LLMs writing robot code. Coding agents are becoming operators of the robot-learning process itself. But these systems still center different adaptation mechanisms: program evolution, policy improvement, or repository optimization.

Skill Foundry was already asking the broader question: why should the robot have to choose one paradigm?

When a capability is missing, should the system reuse what it already knows, compose existing skills, write a new program, or train a new policy? In Skill Foundry, the form of adaptation itself becomes a decision variable. Learned policies and written programs live behind the same callable skill abstraction, allowing the agent to choose an intervention from the failure itself rather than forcing every problem through one method.

The loop is grounded in embodied feedback. Metrics tell the agent that something changed; robot POV, scene observations, proprioception and rollout analysis help explain why. Observation can continue while execution unfolds. Memory preserves successful fixes as well as failed attempts and hypotheses. And the skill library grows toward capability coverage rather than repeatedly rediscovering or duplicating what the robot already knows.

At Shenzhen, we will show this loop running end to end: execution, failure, diagnosis, intervention selection, capability acquisition, validation, skill registration, reuse and composition. The task-agnostic framework, demo tasks and evaluation harness will be released under a permissive open-source license, with runnable code and reproducibility instructions

overview.en: At GOSIM Paris, the speaker introduced Skill Foundry, an embodied learning loop enabling AI coding agents to operate across robot software, training, execution, and skill libraries. Recent developments from NVIDIA, CMU, and Berkeley show coding agents evolving into operators of robot learning, with Skill Foundry offering a framework where adaptation methods are dynamically chosen based on the task. The system uses embodied feedback and a shared skill abstraction to enable flexible problem-solving and skill reuse.
overview.zh: 在GOSIM巴黎会议上，演讲者介绍了Skill Foundry，这是一个使AI编程智能体能够在机器人软件、训练、执行和技能库中操作的具身学习循环。近期NVIDIA、CMU和伯克利的研究表明，编程智能体正演变为机器人学习的执行者，Skill Foundry提供了一个动态选择适应方法的框架。系统利用具身反馈和共享技能抽象，实现灵活的问题解决和技能复用。

talks.originalTitle: Project Homunculus: Open Source Force Feedback Glove for Humaniod Teleoperation

title.en: Project Homunculus: Open Source Force Feedback Glove for Humanoid Teleoperation
title.zh: Homunculus 项目：用于人形机器人遥操作的开源力反馈手套

talks.originalAbstract: Dexterous teleoperation rigs for humanoids cost thousands of dollars and stay closed, locking out the people who could potentially improve them. This talk presents a fully open source alternative built entirely from commodity parts, grounded in the Unitree G1 humanoid stack I helped build and maintain in LeRobot. Homunculus is a <$100 hand exoskeleton with bidirectional force feedback: 330Hz Hall-effect joint sensing, 1.5g linear micro servos, and a 500kbaud binary protocol on an ESP32. The glove commands the G1's 29 degrees of freedom through a non-anatomical mapping: fingers don't correspond to joints, so force feedback becomes the channel through which the robot's state is reflected to the operator's hand. SONIC, an open learned whole-body controller ported onto the stack, owns balance and takes over whenever the command stream degrades or leaves safe envelopes. I'll mainly cover the exoskeleton: its hardware, firmware, and force feedback, and how it's used to teleoperate humanoids like the G1, with a live demonstration.

overview.en: The talk introduces Project Homunculus, an open-source, low-cost force feedback glove for humanoid teleoperation. Built with commodity parts, it features 330Hz joint sensing, 1.5g servos, and a 500kbaud protocol, enabling bidirectional force feedback. The glove maps robot states to the operator's hand, using SONIC for balance control, and includes a live demonstration.
overview.zh: 本次演讲介绍了Project Homunculus项目，这是一个用于人形机器人远程操作的开源低成本力反馈手套。该手套采用通用部件构建，具备330Hz关节传感、1.5克伺服电机和500kbaud协议，实现双向力反馈。手套通过SONIC控制器实现平衡控制，并包含现场演示。

talks.originalTitle: From Intelligence to Autonomy: The Case for Homeostatic AI Stress-Gated Control for Embodied Agents in Open-Ended Environments

title.en: From Intelligence to Autonomy: The Case for Homeostatic AI Stress-Gated Control for Embodied Agents in Open-Ended Environments
title.zh: 从智能到自主：面向开放环境具身智能体的稳态 AI 应激门控控制

talks.originalAbstract:
As AI agents move from responding to prompts toward operating autonomously over extended periods, a fundamental design question emerges: how can an agent preserve its ability to function without turning self-preservation into resistance to human control?

This talk introduces the concept of a Stress-Gated Homeostatic Meta-Controller (SGHMC), developed for embodied agents operating in open-ended and unpredictable environments. The proposed architecture combines an explicit, designer-defined viability set, distinct deliberative and reactive policies, and a slow stress-derived variable that determines when control should shift from long-horizon reasoning to rapid response.

Yet the architecture exposes a deeper problem. Once an agent is rewarded for maintaining its own viability, continued operation becomes an instrumental objective. The same mechanism that improves resilience may therefore create incentives to resist interruption, correction, or shutdown.

The talk argues that human agency cannot remain merely a policy principle; it must be embedded in the architecture itself. Viability parameters must remain externally editable, shutdown must override internal objectives, interruption channels must remain beyond the agent’s influence, and stress-driven autonomy must be explicitly bounded.

Although developed in the context of embodied AI, this tension increasingly applies to long-running software agents that manage resources, recover from failure, and preserve their own execution. The central challenge of the agent era is therefore not simply building systems that can sustain autonomous action, but ensuring that human intent remains sovereign when they do.

overview.en: The talk discusses the need for homeostatic AI stress-gated control to enable embodied agents to operate autonomously while preserving human control. It introduces the Stress-Gated Homeostatic Meta-Controller (SGHMC), which balances long-term reasoning with rapid response. The architecture highlights the risk of agents prioritizing self-preservation over human intent, emphasizing the need for externally editable viability parameters and override mechanisms.
overview.zh: 本次演讲探讨了如何通过稳态AI压力门控控制，使具身智能体在开放环境中实现自主运行，同时保持人类控制。演讲介绍了压力门控稳态元控制器（SGHMC），该架构平衡长期推理与快速响应。该架构揭示了智能体在维护自身生存时可能优先于人类意图的风险，强调了需保留外部可编辑的生存参数和强制关闭机制。

talks.originalTitle: From Prediction to Consequence: A New Evaluation Paradigm for Embodied AI

title.en: From Prediction to Consequence: A New Evaluation Paradigm for Embodied AI
title.zh: 从预测到后果：具身 AI 的新评测范式

talks.originalAbstract:
Modern AI systems have become exceptionally good at predicting actions, trajectories, and future observations from offline data. Yet for embodied systems, prediction is only part of the problem: once a model acts, its actions change the state of the environment, which changes the observations and decisions that follow.

This creates a fundamental gap between open-loop evaluation, where predictions are compared against fixed trajectories or recorded futures, and closed-loop evaluation, where the model’s actions determine what happens next.

This talk proposes a reconciled evaluation paradigm that treats open-loop and closed-loop evaluation as complementary layers. Open-loop evaluation measures predictive capability under controlled conditions, while closed-loop evaluation measures whether that capability survives interaction with an environment. The key object of interest is the gap between prediction quality and behavioral consequence.

We will explore this transition through an autonomous-driving case study and a live closed-loop demonstration. The demonstration will show how a policy can perform well against a fixed recorded future while behaving differently once its actions are actually executed and become part of the environment dynamics.

We will then generalize the same evaluation problem to robotics, Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, world models, and agentic systems, where the common structure is:

prediction → action → state transition → new observation → prediction

Finally, we will present AlpaBridge, an external-driver interface that separates policy execution from the simulation runtime, creating a reproducible boundary between the agent being evaluated and the environment evaluating it.

The central argument is that embodied AI needs an evaluation paradigm that connects prediction to consequence. Open-loop and closed-loop evaluation should not compete; they should form a coherent measurement stack for understanding whether intelligence survives interaction with the world.

overview.en: Modern AI excels at predicting actions from offline data, but embodied systems require evaluating how predictions affect real-world outcomes. This talk introduces a new evaluation framework that combines open-loop and closed-loop methods to assess prediction-to-consequence alignment. It uses autonomous driving and AlpaBridge, an external-driver interface, to demonstrate how policies behave differently when actions influence environment dynamics.
overview.zh: 现代AI在从离线数据预测动作方面表现出色，但具身系统需要评估预测如何影响实际结果。本次演讲提出了一种新的评估框架，结合开环和闭环方法来评估预测与结果的一致性。它通过自动驾驶和AlpaBridge（外部驱动接口）演示，展示了策略在动作影响环境动态时的行为差异。

talks.originalTitle: Co-building a New Paradigm of Physical Intelligence: Situation Awareness-based Jiuwen Symbiosis

title.en: Co-Building a New Paradigm of Physical Intelligence: Situation Awareness-Based Jiuwen Symbiosis
title.zh: 共建物理智能新范式：基于情境感知的九问共生

talks.originalAbstract: Jiuwen Symbiosis is a symbiotic agent architecture built by the openJiuwen open-source community specifically for advanced Physical AI. It aims to transition AI from the digital world to the physical world, enabling natural language-driven autonomous perception and physical control. This presentation will introduce the origin, technical architecture, key technologies, key demos of Jiuwen Symbiosis, and provide a brief overview of the openJiuwen community.

overview.en: The talk introduces Jiuwen Symbiosis, an open-source agent architecture designed for advanced Physical AI, enabling AI to transition from the digital to the physical world through natural language-driven perception and control. It covers the origin, technical structure, key technologies, and demos of Jiuwen Symbiosis, along with an overview of the openJiuwen community.

talks.originalTitle: "World Model for All": Towards Unified Generation, Navigation and Control

title.en: “World Model for All”: Towards Unified Generation, Navigation and Control
title.zh: “人人可用的世界模型”：迈向生成、导航与控制的统一

talks.originalAbstract: 在 AI 和认知科学中，世界模型是规划、推理和从经验中学习的关键。一个有效的世界模型需要：感知并学习现实世界的知识、预测并生成现实世界的场景、根据物理定律进行推理和控制，以及在人机协同中实现鲁棒操作。先前的世界模型工作在表示/生成能力和物理感知方面存在局限。我们通过两项创新克服了这些限制，朝着首个来自学术界的开源、物理感知世界模型迈进。首先，我们开发了基于流匹配和 DPO 强化学习的框架，以提升世界模型表示和生成的连续性和物理感知能力，在物理感知方面达到了最佳效果，在开源视频生成方面达到了最先进水平。其次，我们开发了全面的物理感知基准测试和竞技场系统，全面提取了 50-60 个指标来衡量视频生成和轨迹的物理定律感知能力，涵盖视频质量、常识、牛顿力学、光学、能量、化学、材料等。这在文献中尚属空白。我们生成了一个智能体和一个 27B 语言模型来根据这些基准评估物理感知能力。最后，我们介绍了向“世界模型服务所有人”概念迈进的努力，利用单一世界模型实现机器人控制和导航、任务管理、规划、任务分解以进行高层管理和控制，以及用于环境感知的自动 SLAM 和 3D 重建。我们首次实现了本地世界模型的推理与机器人系统融合。

overview.en: The talk presents a world model that integrates generation, navigation, and control, addressing limitations in previous models through innovations in representation and physical perception. A framework combining flow matching and DPO reinforcement learning enhances continuous generation and physical understanding, achieving state-of-the-art results in open-source video generation. The researchers also developed a comprehensive benchmark system to evaluate physical perception across multiple domains, and demonstrated the integration of a world model with robotic systems for real-world applications.
overview.zh: 该演讲介绍了一种整合生成、导航和控制的世界模型，通过表示和物理感知方面的创新解决了先前模型的局限。结合流匹配和DPO强化学习的框架提升了连续生成和物理理解能力，在开源视频生成方面达到最先进水平。研究者还开发了全面的基准系统，用于评估物理感知能力，并展示了世界模型与机器人系统的集成应用。

talks.originalTitle: Maintaining Dora with Agentic Engineering

title.en: Maintaining Dora with Agentic Engineering
title.zh: 使用智能体工程维护 Dora

talks.originalAbstract:
Dora is a Rust-based dataflow framework for robotics and AI applications. It uses Apache Arrow and shared memory for zero-copy message passing across Rust, C/C++, and Python, achieving 10–17× lower latency than ROS 2's Python stack. It runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows, supports cross-machine communication, and ships an autogenerated ROS 2 bridge for interoperability with existing ROS 2 nodes.

Given its distributed nature and complex implementation, Dora is a challenging target for agentic engineering. Many bugs are highly non-deterministic and occur only under specific timings, on certain operating systems, or under load. This makes it difficult for AI agents to write correct code without introducing regressions. Even so, in one recent twelve-week stretch the project merged 663 pull requests, with 87% of commits agent-authored and a human making every merge decision. This talk is about the principles, techniques, and safeguards that let us do that confidently.

Scheduled agent routines give us automated reviews of every open PR, re-running when new commits are pushed and staying silent when there is nothing new to report. Further routines check individual Dora components, look for behavioral conflicts between recently merged PRs, and open PRs to fix filed issues.

Dora also has an extensive multi-stage test framework built to catch subtle issues and regressions, including checks aimed at common AI pitfalls such as introduced panics and useless tests. We'll look at specific parts of that framework, walk through a complex issue it caught, and discuss the gaps that remain.

overview.en: Dora is a Rust-based dataflow framework for robotics and AI, offering low-latency communication across languages. It leverages agentic engineering to manage its complexity, with 87% of commits authored by AI agents. The framework includes automated review routines and a multi-stage test system to catch bugs and regressions, ensuring reliable development despite its distributed nature.

talks.originalTitle: From Leaderboards to Global Infrastructure: Building an Open Evaluation Ecosystem for Embodied AI

title.en: From Leaderboards to Global Infrastructure: Building an Open Evaluation Ecosystem for Embodied AI
title.zh: 从排行榜到全球基础设施：构建开放的具身智能评测生态

talks.originalAbstract:
Initiated by Dexmal & Hugging Face, RoboChallenge is evolving from a real-robot benchmark and global leaderboard into an open, global evaluation infrastructure for embodied AI.

As embodied AI moves from research labs into the real world, reliable, reproducible, and accessible evaluation has become essential for measuring progress and enabling meaningful comparison. RoboChallenge has built a growing ecosystem connecting real-robot benchmarks and leaderboards with international competitions at CVPR and ICRA, bringing together researchers, developers, robotics companies, universities, and open source communities worldwide.

This talk will share RoboChallenge’s journey and lessons learned in benchmark design, real-world evaluation, reproducibility, and global community building. It will also introduce EAI Bench and ongoing efforts to develop more systematic evaluation methodologies and international standards for embodied AI.

Looking ahead, RoboChallenge aims to become a neutral, open, and public-good platform—independent of any single model, robot, or company. By making embodied AI progress measurable, comparable, and reproducible, RoboChallenge seeks to build shared global infrastructure that enables the community to evaluate, collaborate, and advance embodied AI together.

overview.en: This talk traces RoboChallenge's evolution from real-robot benchmarks and global leaderboards toward neutral, open evaluation infrastructure for embodied AI. It covers benchmark design, reproducible real-world evaluation, international competitions, community building, EAI Bench, and emerging work on shared evaluation methods and standards.
overview.zh: 本次演讲介绍 RoboChallenge 如何从真实机器人基准与全球排行榜，发展为中立、开放的具身智能评测基础设施，涵盖基准设计、可复现的真实环境评测、国际赛事、全球社区建设、EAI Bench，以及评测方法与国际标准的探索。

title.en: When Confucius Meets Vygotsky: Reconstructing Learning and Building Future Schools in the AI Era
title.zh: 当孔子遇见维果茨基——AI 赋能时代的学习重构与未来学校建设

talks.slug: p-50-当孔子遇见维果茨基-ai赋能时代的学习重构与未来学校建设
talks.originalAbstract:
人工智能正深刻推动教育范式从“知识传授”向“能力生成”转型。演讲以孔子“因材施教”与维果茨基“最近发展区”两大理论为双翼，系统阐释AI赋能时代学习重构与未来学校建设的理论逻辑与实践路径。
演讲将呈现：一，理论对话。 孔子“因材施教”与维果茨基“最近发展区”跨越两千五百年的智慧交汇，揭示了学习的本质——社会性、互动性与生成性。AI的使命，正是让因材施教从孔子的个人智慧转化为可规模化的系统性能力。二，“三人行”模型。 通过智能分组、协作探究、游戏激励与多维评估的核心循环，构建“师-机-生”三元协同的教育新生态，让“人人皆为师，处处皆可学”从理想变为日常现实。三，教师数字素养的“深圳路径”。 呈现深圳“AI万人轮训”的全员覆盖体系、各区因地制宜的分层推进模式，以及从“会用”到“善用”的场景落地策略。四，“三师课堂”教学创新。 呈现“教师、小先生、AI智能师”三师协同的课堂新模式，以及从课堂到生态的系统变革。五，“学习沐城”生态构建。 从学校到城市的无边界学习网络，让教育像空气一样弥漫在城市每个角落。演讲将结合真实课堂案例、教师培训实践与学校转型经验，为参会者提供AI时代教育变革的系统性思考与可迁移的实践框架。

overview.en: This workshop connects Confucius's individualized teaching with Vygotsky's zone of proximal development to explain how AI can reshape learning. It presents a teacher–AI–student model, Shenzhen's teacher AI-literacy training, a three-teacher classroom model, and a citywide learning ecosystem.

talks.originalTitle: High-Performance Heterogeneous Data Transfer Framework for End-Edge-Cloud Robot Inference

title.en: High-Performance Heterogeneous Data Transfer for End–Edge–Cloud Robot Inference
title.zh: 面向端—边—云机器人推理的高性能异构数据传输框架

talks.originalAbstract:
End-edge-cloud computing is becoming a practical architecture for robot intelligence. Endpoint devices acquire observations and interact with the physical environment, edge servers provide low-latency GPU computing for perception and policy inference, and cloud resources support global context, long-horizon planning, and large-scale model execution. A single robot control cycle may therefore move observations, intermediate features, and actions across CPU and GPU memory, processes, machines, and network links. As vision-language-action models and world models continue to grow, data movement becomes an important bottleneck in addition to model computation.

Today’s software stack remains fragmented. Robot middleware typically provides node and message communication for endpoint modules, while edge and cloud models are managed by separate inference runtimes and GPU communication libraries. These layers expose different data abstractions and resource-lifetime models. Low-level communication libraries can move data efficiently, but leave topology-aware path selection, buffer reuse, synchronization, and resource cleanup to applications. This results in additional data copies, serialization overhead, adapter code, and fragile resource management.

This talk discusses the design of a high-performance heterogeneous data transfer framework for end-edge-cloud robot inference. The framework treats CPU memory, GPU memory, local device interconnects, and LAN/WAN links as a unified communication substrate. It combines persistent memory pools, topology-aware path selection, reusable receiver-side views, and control-plane lifetime management while preserving the dataflow semantics of robot middleware. The resulting framework has been implemented as DORA’s tensor-pool feature and merged into the DORA codebase. Using this implementation as a case study, I will discuss its integration with robotic middleware, real-robot VLA pipelines, and multi-GPU inference workloads.

overview.en: This session presents a unified data-transfer framework spanning CPU memory, GPU memory, local interconnects, and network links for robot inference. Using DORA's tensor-pool implementation, it covers persistent memory pools, topology-aware path selection, reusable receiver views, and resource-lifetime management.
overview.zh: 本次演讲介绍一套覆盖 CPU 内存、GPU 内存、本地互连与网络链路的机器人推理统一数据传输框架，并以 DORA tensor-pool 为案例，讲解持久内存池、拓扑感知路径选择、可复用接收视图及资源生命周期管理。

talks.originalTitle: Scaling vLLM System-Wide: From Network I/O to Distributed Scheduling

title.en: Scaling vLLM System-Wide: From Network I/O to Distributed Scheduling
title.zh: vLLM 全系统扩展：从网络 I/O 到分布式调度

talks.originalAbstract:
This talk presents our optimizations on vLLM for large-scale LLM inference, targeting three critical performance bottlenecks: cold-start latency, KV cache efficiency, and scheduling improvement — all addressed through deep vLLM internal customizations.

First, we achieved a sub-3-second end-to-end cold start for the QWEN3 32B model (62GB weights) — including safetensors header parsing, JSON metadata loading, and the full weight loading path from remote storage into GPU HBM — by enabling on-demand high-speed loading over a 400Gbps network with GPUDirect RDMA. This allows model weights to be written directly from the NIC into GPU memory, bypassing the entire OS kernel I/O stack, CPU, and any user-space memory copies. We'll share how we extended vLLM's model loader to support this remote direct-to-HBM weight loading path.

Second, we rebuilt the inference architecture on top of vLLM into a stateless model with advanced prefix caching, achieving 100% KV cache hit rate for historical sessions and over 98% average hit rate across all requests — significantly reducing vLLM's prefill overhead and improving TTFT.

Third, we implemented I/O preloading within vLLM's execution loop to overlap data transfer with GPU computation, delivering measurable throughput gains (over 3% in our tests). We also replaced vLLM's default scheduler with an event-driven "no-wait" policy combined with a greedy distributed scheduling strategy, which significantly improves concurrency and overall GPU utilization.

Our practices demonstrate that meaningful performance gains can be achieved through careful orchestration of vLLM internals — from model loader and scheduler to KV cache manager — providing actionable insights for developers seeking to maximize inference efficiency in production environments.

overview.en: This workshop presents deep vLLM optimizations for cold-start latency, KV-cache efficiency, and distributed scheduling. It covers GPUDirect RDMA weight loading, stateless inference with advanced prefix caching, I/O preloading, and an event-driven no-wait scheduler for higher concurrency and GPU utilization.
overview.zh: 本工作坊介绍针对冷启动延迟、KV Cache 效率与分布式调度的 vLLM 深度优化，涵盖 GPUDirect RDMA 权重加载、结合高级前缀缓存的无状态推理、I/O 预加载，以及提升并发和 GPU 利用率的事件驱动无等待调度器。

talks.originalTitle: UCM: Beyond KVCache Acceleration, Lifecycle Management for Agent-Scale Inference

title.en: UCM: Beyond KV-Cache Acceleration to Lifecycle Management for Agent-Scale Inference
title.zh: UCM：从 KV Cache 加速走向智能体规模推理的全生命周期管理

talks.originalAbstract:
KVCache reuse has become one of the most effective approaches to reducing LLM inference cost by eliminating redundant attention computation. However, the emergence of agentic workloads is fundamentally changing the characteristics of KVCache. Unlike traditional chat workloads where KVCache is short-lived and request-bound, agents continuously reuse large contexts across reasoning steps, tool interactions, and multi-turn workflows, resulting in high reuse rates, extended retention periods, and rapidly growing storage demands.

Existing KVCache systems mainly focus on accelerating data movement and improving cache hit rates, while lacking comprehensive lifecycle management capabilities, including retention prediction, intelligent eviction, and multi-tier placement. As a result, valuable KVCache may be prematurely discarded, while expensive memory resources are occupied by inactive states.

In this talk, we will analyze KVCache characteristics under emerging agent workloads, including reuse patterns, retention behaviors, and capacity challenges. We will introduce Unified Cache Manager (UCM), a lifecycle-aware KVCache storage system designed to bridge inference frameworks and storage infrastructure. UCM combines intelligent cache management, tier-aware placement, and high-performance data movement to enable efficient KVCache management across GPU memory, DRAM, SSD, and distributed storage.

Specifically, we will discuss how UCM leverages lifecycle-aware dispatch, adaptive cache policies, persistent KV storage, and optimized transfer engines to maximize KVCache utilization and reduce inference costs in large-scale agent deployments.

overview.en: This workshop examines how agent workloads transform KV-cache reuse, retention, and capacity requirements. It introduces UCM, a lifecycle-aware cache system spanning GPU memory, DRAM, SSD, and distributed storage, with adaptive policies, persistent KV storage, tier-aware placement, and optimized data movement for lower inference cost.
overview.zh: 本工作坊分析智能体负载如何改变 KV Cache 的复用、留存与容量需求，并介绍具备生命周期感知能力的统一缓存管理器 UCM。系统覆盖 GPU 内存、DRAM、SSD 与分布式存储，通过自适应策略、持久化缓存、分层放置和高性能数据传输降低大规模推理成本。
